target.title: fix(ollama): use CJK-aware char estimate for usage fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama's chat stream reports real usage via `prompt_eval_count`/`eval_count`
on the final response chunk. When those fields are missing or invalid (e.g. a
native stream that ends early), `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts` falls back
to estimating tokens as `chars / 4` using plain UTF-16 `.length` on the
message content, tool-call JSON, and tool names.

That heuristic assumes ~4 chars/token, which holds for Latin/English text but
badly undercounts CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) text, which tokenizes at
roughly 1 char/token. For CJK-heavy conversations that hit this fallback path,
usage is undercounted by 2-4x.

This fallback usage feeds `assistantMessage.usage`, which is used both for
usage/context telemetry (`/context`, treemap, totals) and for
`calculateContextTokens` → `shouldCompact` proactive context-window
compaction decisions. Undercounting on CJK sessions means the agent believes
it has more context headroom than it actually does, delaying proactive
compaction until the provider itself errors on overflow.

## Why This Change Was Made

The core already has the correct weighting formula in `src/utils/cjk-chars.ts`
(`estimateStringChars`). Ollama's extension cannot import core internals, and
exposing that helper through the public plugin SDK would create a new stable
API commitment for a single consumer. This change mirrors the core weighting
locally in `extensions/ollama/src/cjk-char-estimate.ts` and applies it on the
production stream fallback path only.

This change:
- Weights message content, tool names, serialized tool fields, and completion
  text with the CJK-aware char estimate before the existing `chars / 4`
  rounding.
- Leaves provider-reported `prompt_eval_count` / `eval_count` authoritative
  when present.
- Proves the production caller path over real loopback HTTP (no fetch mock):
  `createOllamaStreamFn` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → NDJSON final chunk without
  eval counts → `done.message.usage`.

## User Impact

No change for ASCII/Latin content (the fallback estimate is unchanged for
that case). For CJK-heavy Ollama conversations that hit the native-usage
fallback path, usage/context accounting and proactive compaction triggering
are now accurate instead of undercounting by 2-4x. When Ollama does report
valid eval counts, those values remain authoritative.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts`,
  `extensions/ollama/src/cjk-char-estimate.ts`,
  `extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts`,
  `extensions/ollama/src/stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts`
- Production caller path: `createOllamaStreamFn` → guarded fetch → NDJSON parse →
  fallback estimators → `buildAssistantMessage` → `done.message.usage`
- Compatibility: provider-reported eval counts still win over the fallback
- No public plugin-SDK export added

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

When an Ollama-shaped NDJSON stream's final chunk omits `prompt_eval_count` /
`eval_count`, the production stream path writes CJK-aware fallback usage onto
`done.message.usage` (roughly 1 token per CJK char) instead of the old raw
UTF-16 `length / 4` undercount. Valid provider-reported eval counts still
override the fallback.

### Canonical reachability path

`createOllamaStreamFn` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `/api/chat` NDJSON final chunk
without eval counts → `estimateOllamaPromptTokens` /
`estimateOllamaCompletionTokens` → `buildAssistantMessage` →
`done.message.usage`

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Local `estimateStringChars` mirrors `src/utils/cjk-chars.ts` so the extension
stays inside the plugin boundary without growing the public SDK surface.
Provider-reported eval counts remain authoritative via `resolveUsageCount`.

### Real environment tested

Real HTTP transport: local `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1` speaking Ollama
NDJSON `/api/chat`. The production `createOllamaStreamFn` path uses the real
`fetchWithSsrFGuard` (no SSRF mock) against that live socket. Final chunk
omits eval counts to force the fallback; sibling case keeps
`prompt_eval_count=77` / `eval_count=19` to prove provider counts stay
authoritative. Node v22.23.1.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts \
  extensions/ollama/src/stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts > createOllamaStreamFn thinking events > falls back to CJK-aware usage when the final chunk omits eval counts 1ms
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts > createOllamaStreamFn thinking events > keeps provider-reported eval counts authoritative over the CJK fallback 0ms
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts > createOllamaStreamFn thinking events > matches the plain chars/4 heuristic for ASCII-only fallback usage 0ms
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/ollama/src/stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts > createOllamaStreamFn CJK usage fallback (real HTTP) > estimates CJK-aware usage when a real Ollama-shaped stream omits eval counts 28ms
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/ollama/src/stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts > createOllamaStreamFn CJK usage fallback (real HTTP) > keeps provider-reported eval counts authoritative over the HTTP fallback 4ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  21 passed (21)
```

### Observed result after fix

Against a live loopback Ollama NDJSON server (real guarded fetch, no mock), a
CJK prompt/completion whose final chunk omits eval counts yields fallback
`usage.input` / `usage.output` that match `estimateStringChars(...)/4` and are
more than 2x the naive `length/4` undercount. When the final chunk includes
valid eval counts, those exact provider numbers are preserved on
`done.message.usage`.

### What was not tested

Live generation against a real Ollama daemon binary. The fallback trigger proven
here is the same production path that runs after NDJSON parse when eval counts
are absent or invalid; a daemon that always emits counts would not enter this
path without an intervening strip/proxy.

### Fix classification

bugfix — usage accounting / CJK undercount

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the local CJK mirror (no public SDK export),
real-HTTP caller-path proof, and CI unused-export cleanup.

target.title: fix(doctor): keep failure report truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

`sanitizeFailureReportText` in `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.ts` truncates the failure report text to 500 characters after redacting sensitive data. The truncation uses `.slice(0, 500)` which can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair if the 500-char boundary falls between a pair. Replaced with `truncateUtf16Safe` to ensure surrogate pair integrity. Also refactored to use a clean cap + marker pattern instead of inline `.slice(0, 500)`.

What changed: The `.slice(0, 500)` at the end of `sanitizeFailureReportText` replaced with `truncateUtf16Safe(redacted, cap - marker.length) + marker` pattern, where marker is `"... [truncated]"`. The import of `truncateUtf16Safe` added.

What NOT changed: Redaction logic (email, API key, token patterns) unchanged. Return type unchanged. All existing behavior for sub-500-char reports preserved.

Fixes #109981

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When a doctor failure report exceeds 500 characters after redaction and contains surrogate pair characters (e.g., emoji like 😀) at the truncation boundary, the resulting report has an invalid dangling surrogate rendering as garbled text, which can break downstream consumers (DB storage, JSON serialization, etc.).

**Root Cause**: `sanitizeFailureReportText` at `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.ts:983` uses `.slice(0, 500)`, which operates on UTF-16 code units and can split a surrogate pair at position 500.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, 500)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(redacted, cap - marker.length)` so the truncation never splits a surrogate pair. The marker length is subtracted from the cap to include the `"... [truncated]"` suffix within the 500-char target.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic / Node.js v25.9.0 / pnpm tsx v4.22.4, commit 339041101b0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsx tmp-utf16-evidence.mjs` -- exercise the same `sanitizeFailureReportText` + `truncateUtf16Safe` logic against text containing PII (email, token) and multi-byte characters (emoji, CJK) at or past the 500-char truncation boundary.

**After-fix evidence**:

```
HEAD: 339041101b00018000953ac682f099aed63efbed

1. Proof: .slice(0, N) produces a lone surrogate
  text length: 502, slice(0,500): 500 chars
  >> LONE SURROGATE at index 499 -- breaks downstream consumers

2. Short text -- no truncation: OK (32 chars, no change)

3. Long text with PII + emoji -- redaction & truncation
  input: 893, output: 500, truncated: true
  email redacted: true, token redacted: true
  PASS: no unpaired surrogate

4. Boundary -- exactly 500 chars with trailing emoji: PASS

5. Long text -- emoji at truncation boundary: PASS

6. Realistic -- CJK text + emoji + PII: PASS
  email redacted: true, truncated: true, no unpaired surrogate

7. Before/After comparison -- .slice vs truncateUtf16Safe: PASS
  BEFORE (.slice): len=500, unpaired=NONE (but can split pairs)
  AFTER (truncateUtf16Safe): len=500, unpaired=NONE (guaranteed safe)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 7 scenarios pass. No unpaired surrogates in any test case. The `truncateUtf16Safe` function guarantees no broken characters regardless of where the 500-char boundary falls, while `.slice()` produces a lone surrogate when a surrogate pair straddles the boundary.

**What was not tested**: Real Gateway process invoking the doctor migration failure path end-to-end. The change is a pure function swap at the string level.

## Tests and validation

```
PASS: .slice(0, 500) traps lone surrogate when boundary splits a pair
PASS: sanitizeFailureReportText with truncateUtf16Safe -- short text (no-op)
PASS: sanitizeFailureReportText with truncateUtf16Safe -- long text, PII redaction, truncation
PASS: sanitizeFailureReportText with truncateUtf16Safe -- exactly at 500-char boundary with emoji
PASS: sanitizeFailureReportText with truncateUtf16Safe -- emoji at truncation boundary
PASS: sanitizeFailureReportText with truncateUtf16Safe -- realistic CJK + emoji + PII
PASS: Before/after comparison -- truncateUtf16Safe never produces lone surrogates
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

target.title: fix(channels): stale presence after installing a persisted-auth channel plugin
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators who dynamically install (or uninstall, enable/disable, or reload) a plugin that adds a channel with persisted auth state (for example a bundled Matrix/Signal-style channel) would keep seeing the pre-mutation channel presence list. Callers that rely on `config-presence` without passing a fresh discovery result (such as `openclaw doctor` and other non-discovery presence checks) continued to report the stale set of "potentially configured" channels for the lifetime of the process, so a freshly installed channel could be missing from presence output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The module-level `persistedAuthStateChannelIds` cache in `src/channels/config-presence.ts` was populated on first use and never invalidated, so it could not observe registry changes at runtime. The cache is documented as stale after *any* registry mutation or config reload, not only after an installed-package install.

Instead of calling the invalidation from a single install path, this wires `invalidatePersistedAuthStateCache()` into `refreshPluginRegistryAfterConfigMutation` in `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts` — the single committed boundary that install, uninstall, enable/disable, and config reload all funnel through (via `install-persistence.ts`, `management-service.ts`, `plugins-uninstall-command.ts`, and the update paths). Invalidating there means every registry mutation clears the persisted-auth presence cache, so the next presence scan re-reads bundled plugin metadata. No config shape, protocol, or public presence API changes; the cache remains a process-local single slot.

## User Impact

After dynamically installing, uninstalling, or reloading a plugin that contributes a persisted-auth channel, presence detection (including `openclaw doctor`) now reflects the current channel set without requiring a gateway restart.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `src/channels/config-presence.test.ts`:
  - Mocked lifecycle tests reproduce the stale-cache behavior across install, uninstall, and multi-cycle mutations, asserting the cache resets and the next read returns the updated channel list.
  - A **real (non-mocked) wiring test** imports the actual shared boundary `refreshPluginRegistryAfterConfigMutation` and asserts it invokes `invalidatePersistedAuthStateCache()` — proving the invalidation is reached through the production registry-mutation path, not just a manually called helper.
- Focused suite green locally (current rebased head):

  ```
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/config-presence.test.ts
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  10 passed (10)
  ```

- oxlint clean; `registry-refresh.ts` import path resolves (`../channels/config-presence.js`).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: `src/channels/config-presence.ts` kept a module-level `persistedAuthStateChannelIds` cache that was populated on first use and never invalidated. After an operator installed/uninstalled/reloaded a channel plugin with persisted auth at runtime, presence callers that did not pass a fresh discovery result (e.g. `openclaw doctor`) kept reporting the stale pre-mutation channel list for the process lifetime. The fix adds `invalidatePersistedAuthStateCache()` and calls it from `refreshPluginRegistryAfterConfigMutation` — the shared registry-mutation boundary used by install, uninstall, enable/disable, and config reload.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0, vitest 4.1.10. The invalidation seam is covered by `src/channels/config-presence.test.ts`, including a real-boundary test that drives `refreshPluginRegistryAfterConfigMutation` (no mocked config-presence source) and asserts the cache is invalidated.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/config-presence.test.ts`

Evidence after fix: The `Real behavior proof` CI check passed for this head. The suite adds both mocked lifecycle coverage (`+106` lines in `config-presence.test.ts`) and a real-boundary assertion, and `registry-refresh.ts` calls the new seam inside the shared mutation boundary (`+10`).

Observed result after fix: A freshly installed/uninstalled channel with persisted auth now appears (or disappears) in presence output on the next read after any registry mutation, instead of being hidden behind a stale cached set.

What was not tested: A full multi-plugin gateway restart was not run; the proof targets the exact changed seam — the cache invalidation on the shared registry-mutation boundary and its effect on the next presence derivation.

target.title: fix(hooks): serialize same-session agent hook dispatch to prevent silent event loss from session-claim races
target.body:
Closes #110109

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multiple agent-hook events targeting the same `sessionKey` within a short window were silently dropped when `cron.maxConcurrentRuns > 1`. The hooks executed concurrently and raced on the optimistic session claim: the first winner claimed the session; the rest threw `CronSessionLifecycleClaimError`, which was caught by `dispatchAgentHook`'s error handler and recorded as a system event with no retry. The hook events and their payloads were permanently lost.

Impact (from the issue reporter): "…observed in production dropping ~12 wakes/day, including the events that were supposed to launch coding agents in response to PR review feedback."

## Why This Change Was Made

`dispatchAgentHook` now serializes same-session dispatch through a per-`sessionKey` promise chain. Each hook's async body awaits the previous hook for that session before its cron run starts, so concurrent events targeting one session execute sequentially without claim races. Different sessions still dispatch in parallel — the serialization is keyed on `sessionKey`. The `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation` wrapper, hook naming, error handling, and system-event reporting are all unchanged.

## User Impact

Webhook bursts that deliver multiple events for one session (e.g., a GitHub PR review + inline comments, or an issue-tracker delegate-change + state-change) no longer silently drop events when `maxConcurrentRuns > 1`. Each event runs sequentially into the session.

Setting `maxConcurrentRuns: 1` continues to serialize all hooks globally and is not affected.

## Evidence

### Regression coverage

- Existing `hooks.agent-trust.test.ts` (10 tests) passes unchanged — the gateway-independent continuation, admission accounting, untrusted-name sanitization, and non-ok/warning/reporting contracts are preserved.
- New `serializes same-session hook dispatch so no claim race occurs` test: dispatches two same-session hooks where the first blocks on a gate; asserts the second has not started cron execution until the first is released. Against unfixed `main`, this test fails (both hooks start concurrently and race).
- New `serializes same-session hook dispatch` test: confirms the chain ordering with a mock-implementation that gates the first and releases after the second is dispatched.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server/hooks.agent-trust.test.ts` → 12 passed.
- Scoped `check-test-types`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` pass on the two changed files.

### Runtime behavior proof (live gateway admission)

The production `dispatchAgentHook` closure from hooks.ts (the exact function wired by `createGatewayHooksRequestHandler`, not a test double) was exercised through a live gateway work-admission root created via `tryBeginGatewayRootWorkAdmission`. Both same-session hooks were dispatched from inside the admission context, then the admission was released (simulating the HTTP request completing while hook work is detached). The first hook entered its cron run; the second was queued behind the per-sessionKey chain and only started after the first hook's gate was released. Terminal output from the production code path:

```
[proof] dispatching first hook from inside admission root
[proof] active roots after first dispatch: 2
[proof] dispatching second hook (same sessionKey)
[proof] active roots after second dispatch: 3
[proof] request admission released (hook work is detached)
[proof] first hook entered and gated — started=[first]
[proof] releasing first-hook gate
[proof] first hook completed — chain advances
[proof] second hook entered — started=[first,second]
[proof] PASS — both hooks serialized by production sessionDispatchChains, no claim race
```

Only the cron runner is gated for observation; every other function, closure, Promise chain, and admission-accounting path is the exact production artifact from `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`.

target.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadCronQuarantineFile` in `src/cron/store.ts` reads the cron quarantine sidecar with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A corrupted or hostile quarantine file could force the cron load path to buffer an arbitrarily large file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Quarantine sidecars are small JSON files. An 8 MiB cap is generous headroom for legitimate quarantine state while preventing the cron load path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector. When the sidecar exceeds the cap during writes, it is archived and a fresh file is started so SQLite persistence continues.

## Changes

1. **Bounded reads**: `loadCronQuarantineFile` uses the shared `readRegularFile` helper with an 8 MiB cap instead of unbounded `fs.promises.readFile`.
2. **Bounded writes**: `saveCronQuarantineFile` checks the serialized payload size before writing. If it exceeds 8 MiB, the existing file is archived and a fresh file with only the new entries is created. If a single entry alone exceeds the cap, writes fail with a clear error.
3. **Archive retention**: Archived sidecar files use a fixed name (`*.archive.json`), so repeated overflows overwrite the previous archive instead of creating an unbounded collection of uniquely named files that can exhaust disk.
4. **Tests**: Regression coverage for bounded reads, oversized write rejection, archive creation and fresh-start recovery, and single-archive retention after repeated overflows.

## User Impact

A corrupted or oversized quarantine sidecar is rejected before OOM. When the sidecar grows past 8 MiB during cron operations, the overflow is archived and a fresh sidecar is started, keeping cron persistence alive. Archives do not accumulate.

## Evidence

### Real test output: all 6 PR-specific tests pass

The actual `src/cron/store.test.ts` test suite was run against the PR's code. All 6 quarantine-related tests pass, demonstrating bounded reads, write rejection, archive rotation, and single-archive retention. The sole test failure is a SQLite-dependent pre-existing test (`lets doctor import legacy top-level array jobs into SQLite and archive the source`) that cannot run locally due to Node 24.13.1's embedded SQLite 3.51.2 (the code requires SQLite 3.51.3+ for WAL safety).

```
 ✓ |cron| fails closed instead of overwriting unrecognized quarantine files
 ✓ |cron| rejects oversized quarantine files to prevent OOM
 ✓ |cron| rejects writing a quarantine sidecar that would exceed the byte cap
 ✓ |cron| archives an existing quarantine sidecar and starts fresh when the cap is exceeded
 ✓ |cron| keeps only one archive after repeated overflows
 ✓ |cron| does not rewrite quarantine files when every entry is already present

 Tests:  1 failed (SQLite-dependent pre-existing test), 6 passed, 44 skipped
```

The 6 passing tests directly exercise the PR's bounded read (`readRegularFile` with 8 MiB cap), bounded write (payload size check before persistence), archive rotation (oversized sidecar archived, fresh file started), and single-archive retention (`*.archive.json` overwritten on repeated overflow).

### Subsystem warning output (via rawConsole capture)

When `loadCronQuarantineFile` encounters an oversized file, the subsystem logger emits a warn-level message through the `cron/store` subsystem:

```
[WARN] [cron/store] Quarantine file at .../cron-quarantine.json exceeds the 8388608-byte limit
```

The quarantine file is rejected and the cron load path continues without loading the corrupted state.

target.title: fix: stop model fallback on sandbox provisioning failures
target.body:
Closes #106516

AI-assisted: implemented with Codex and independently reviewed with the repository autoreview workflow (Claude fallback after both Codex reviewer models failed before returning a verdict).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running sandboxed agents would consume every configured model fallback when the sandbox backend could not start, such as when a Docker sandbox image was missing. The same local provisioning failure was repeated as model fallback activity instead of surfacing once as the actionable runtime error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sandbox backend creation now wraps startup failures in a typed `SandboxProvisioningError`. The existing non-provider runtime classification handles that type before fallback candidate accounting, without matching Docker error text, while explicit provider status/code errors retain provider-fallback precedence.

## User Impact

Sandbox provisioning failures now stop after the first attempt, emit no model-fallback transition diagnostics, and preserve a clear backend startup message for the child run and parent completion path. Legitimate provider/model failures continue to use configured fallbacks.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the focused regression run failed because the same provisioning error invoked two model candidates and backend creation exposed only a plain `Error`.
- After the fix and rebase onto current `main`, Node 24.16.0 passed:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts src/agents/failover-error.test.ts src/agents/sandbox.resolveSandboxContext.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-output.test.ts`
  - 4 files, 260 tests passed across 2 Vitest shards.
- Regression coverage verifies:
  - one model attempt and zero `model.failover` diagnostics;
  - typed backend startup failure with the original cause and actionable message;
  - explicit provider classification still wins over a nested provisioning error;
  - failed child wait state preserves the actionable provisioning error in parent completion findings.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.
- `pnpm check:loc --base origin/main --head HEAD` passed after CI caught the initial legacy-file LOC growth; `src/agents/failover-error.ts` is now two lines smaller than `main`.
- Mandatory autoreview was clean against the full production diff and the final parent-visibility test; no actionable findings remain. The Codex reviewer runtime failed before a verdict after three identical retries, while the supported Claude fallback returned clean results.

target.title: fix: failed cloud dispatch leaks the session's managed worktree
target.body:
Related: #110224

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where choosing a Cloud target in the New Session composer and hitting a dispatch rejection (for example "cloud worker dispatch requires the OpenClaw runtime, not codex") would clean up the just-created session but permanently leak its session-owned managed worktree and branch on disk, with no owning session left in the session list. It also lets operators hit that runtime rejection blind: the Cloud target was offered even when the configured agent runtime can never dispatch.

Found during a live stress test of cloud workers on a dev gateway with the bundled crabbox provider (see the linked issue for the full session log).

## Why This Change Was Made

Two bounded changes:

1. Session deletion now snapshots and removes session-owned managed worktrees instead of relying on the lossless check. The previous `removeIfLossless` gate can never pass in a workspace repo with no git remote (its `git log HEAD --not --remotes` treats the entire inherited history as unpushed), so every session delete preserved an ownerless checkout. `remove()` already snapshots the working tree into `refs/openclaw/snapshots/<id>` before removal, so content stays restorable; on cleanup failure the preserved checkout is still reported.
2. The New Session composer resolves the effective agent runtime from configured model metadata and disables the Cloud target with an explanatory tooltip ("Cloud workers require the OpenClaw runtime; {runtime} is selected.") and blocks submission when it is not `openclaw`. Note the limitation: implicit provider-side routing (e.g. OpenAI models auto-routing to the Codex runtime without any configured `agentRuntime`) is not visible to the UI, so the server-side dispatch check remains the authority; this pre-check catches the configured cases.

## User Impact

Failed cloud dispatches no longer litter the workspace with orphaned worktrees/branches, and session deletion reliably cleans up its worktree while keeping a restorable snapshot. Operators with a configured non-OpenClaw runtime see why Cloud is unavailable up front instead of a post-creation failure banner.

## Evidence

- Live repro before the fix: dispatch rejected with the codex-runtime error left `wt-3f8d623c` + branch `openclaw/wt-3f8d623c` on disk with no owning session.
- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts ui/src/pages/new-session/cloud-target.test.ts ui/src/pages/new-session/model-control.test.ts` — gateway shard 24 passed, UI shard 34 passed. The lifecycle test now proves the worktree registration and branch are gone after delete and a `refs/openclaw/snapshots/` ref is recorded.
- Structured autoreview (codex, gpt-5.6-sol): clean, no actionable findings.

Fixes an issue where the openclaw-release-checks workflow could remain stuck in either of its two `git fetch` steps until the job timeout when the Git transport stalls. This blocks release validation checks and wastes runner time.

This matches the pattern already applied to Mantis Crabbox workflows in #108940 (commit 16c2bbb). All release-check logic and non-network operations are unchanged.

## User Impact

Maintainers get prompt, actionable fetch failures instead of losing a release-checks runner for the full job timeout before validation begins.

target.title: fix(gateway): scope accumulatedText preservation to media-only replace events
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multimodal agent users on the OpenResponses gateway would see their assistant reply silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emitted a media-only SSE replace event (`replace: true`, `text: ""`) during streaming.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old guard `typeof text === "string"` treated empty string as valid content, unconditionally resetting `accumulatedText` on any `replace: true` event. The fix scopes accumulated-text preservation to media-bearing replacement events by checking for non-empty `mediaUrls`/`mediaUrl` — the same media-content signal used by the existing SSE coalesce path (`server-chat.ts:1101`). Non-media empty-text replacement continues to clear the buffer per existing behavior.

## User Impact

Users of multimodal agents (image+text input) on the OpenResponses gateway no longer see their assistant replies silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emits a media-only replace event during streaming.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested**: Ubuntu 24.04, Node 22.22.3 (SQLite 3.51.3), branch `fix/bug-001-accumulatedText-empty-replace` (rebased to latest `origin/main` at `7c262eaae7f`)
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts
  ```

- **Evidence after fix (rebased)**:

  ```
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  35 passed (35)
  ```

  All 35 OpenResponses gateway tests pass on the rebased branch.

- **Shared code alignment.** The agent runtime producer (`agent-runner-execution.ts:2604`) already guards `replace: true` with a truthy `snapshotText` check. The runtime path at `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:1450` produces the exact `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...] }` + `replace: true` event shape that this fix targets.

- **What was not tested**: Non-streaming paths (not affected — `accumulatedText` is streaming-only). Real multimodal provider E2E flow (the event shape is produced by the agent runtime, not the provider directly; the mock test exercises the exact runtime event sequence).

### Standalone proof script

A self-contained proof script exercising the **exact algorithm** from `openresponses-http.ts:1049-1059` is available at [`scripts/proof-openresponses-media-replace.mjs`](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/openclaw/blob/fix/bug-001-accumulatedText-empty-replace/scripts/proof-openresponses-media-replace.mjs). It requires no OpenClaw runtime — just `node scripts/proof-openresponses-media-replace.mjs`:

```
$ node scripts/proof-openresponses-media-replace.mjs

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  Proof: OpenResponses Media-Only Replace Event                  ║
║  Algorithm: openresponses-http.ts:1049-1059 (hasMediaContent)    ║
║  Producer:  embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:1450   ║
║  Event:     { text:"", replace:true, mediaUrls:[...] }          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

  ------------------------------------------------------------------
    [media-preserve        ] REPLACE text="" hasMedia=true  media=["https://example.com/image.jpg"] → PRESERVE (buffer="Hello world")
    [media-preserve        ] FINALIZE phase=end accumulatedText="Hello world" → finalText="Hello world"

  ------------------------------------------------------------------
    [media-empty-array     ] REPLACE text="" hasMedia=false media=[]  → CLEAR→SET
    [media-empty-array     ] FINALIZE phase=end accumulatedText=""    → finalText="No response from OpenClaw."

  ------------------------------------------------------------------
    [media-empty-string    ] REPLACE text="" hasMedia=false media=""  → CLEAR→SET
    [media-empty-string    ] FINALIZE phase=end accumulatedText=""    → finalText="No response from OpenClaw."

  ------------------------------------------------------------------
    [normal-replace        ] REPLACE text="Replaced text" hasMedia=false → SET
    [normal-replace        ] FINALIZE phase=end accumulatedText="Replaced text" → finalText="Replaced text"

  ------------------------------------------------------------------
    [multi-content         ] REPLACE text="" hasMedia=true media=["https://example.com/img1.png"] → PRESERVE (buffer="Hello world")
    [multi-content         ] REPLACE text="" hasMedia=true media=["https://example.com/img2.png"] → PRESERVE (buffer="Hello world")
    [multi-content         ] FINALIZE phase=end accumulatedText="Hello world" → finalText="Hello world"

  ✓ media-preserve: Hello world
  ✓ media-empty-array: No response from OpenClaw.
  ✓ media-empty-string: No response from OpenClaw.
  ✓ normal-replace: Replaced text
  ✓ multi-content: Hello world
  PROOF VERDICT: ALL PASSED ✓
```

The trace confirms five distinct behaviors:
1. Empty text **with** valid `mediaUrls` → accumulated text **preserved**
2. Empty text with empty `mediaUrls: []` → buffer **cleared** (unchanged behavior)
3. Empty text with empty `mediaUrl: ""` → buffer **cleared** (unchanged behavior)
4. Non-empty text (normal replacement) → `accumulatedText` **set** to new text
5. Multiple media blocks (2 images) → each **preserves** buffer

### Integrated behavior proof (before vs after)

The fix was verified by temporarily reverting the guard condition and re-running the same test suite:

**Before (old guard — bug):**
```
 FAIL  |gateway-methods| OpenResponses HTTP API (e2e) > preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
AssertionError: expected 'No response from OpenClaw.' to be 'Hello world'

Expected: "Hello world"
Received: "No response from OpenClaw."
```

3 tests failed across 3 gateway shards — all returning `"No response from OpenClaw."` instead of the expected `"Hello world"`.

**After (PR guard — fixed):**
```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  35 passed (35)
```

All 35 tests pass, including all 3 regression tests for the media-bearing replace path.

### Guard condition summary

```
Event shape                                | main (bug)      | PR (fixed)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Empty text + valid mediaUrls             | REPLACE (bug!)  | PRESERVE ✓
Empty text + mediaUrls:[]                | REPLACE         | REPLACE ✓
Empty text + mediaUrl:''                 | REPLACE         | REPLACE ✓
Non-empty text (normal replacement)      | REPLACE         | REPLACE ✓
Multiple media blocks (2 images)         | REPLACE (bug!)  | PRESERVE ✓
```

The agent runtime producer code proves that `{ text: "", replace: true, mediaUrls: [...] }` is always a media-only addition, never an intentional text deletion.

### Regression test plan

3 regression tests cover the behavioral surface:
1. Valid `mediaUrls` → text preserved
2. Empty `mediaUrls: []` → text cleared (existing behavior)
3. Empty `mediaUrl: ""` → text cleared (existing behavior)

All 35 gateway tests pass with zero regression on the latest `origin/main`.

target.title: fix(ui): Skills page shows Unavailable security badges because verdicts never hydrate on first load
target.body:
Closes #108647

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Control UI Skills page showed a yellow **Unavailable** security badge for linked ClawHub skills on first load, even when the gateway's `skills.securityVerdicts` already reported `ok=true / decision=pass / securityStatus=clean`. The badge implied a broken or unverified skill when only the UI's verdict cache was empty.

## Why This Change Was Made

The route loader hydrates the `skills.status` report but never fetches security verdicts, and `ensureInitialData()` short-circuits once route data is present — so the only code path that populates `clawhubVerdicts` (`loadSkills` → `loadClawHubSecurityVerdicts`) never ran on first paint. Additionally nothing retried: if the verdict loader ran while `connected` was transiently false it cleared the map silently.

The fix exports the existing `loadClawHubSecurityVerdicts` helper and (1) calls it from `applyRouteData()` whenever the route provides a report, reusing the exact production loader (no-linked-skills fast path, agent-scope guards, error handling included), and (2) backfills from `ensureInitialData()` — invoked on every gateway state change — whenever a report is loaded but the verdict map is empty; the helper's early return keeps this RPC-free when no linked ClawHub skills exist.

The branch is rebuilt on current `main` after the Web Awesome Control UI refactor (#106865): the earlier revision of this PR also fixed `applyRouteData()` copying a stale loader-time `connected:false` over the live connection state, which is exactly the "client present while `connected === false`" observation in the issue; `main` now reads `connected` from the live gateway snapshot itself, so that part of the fix is already absorbed and no longer in this diff.

## User Impact

Skills page security badges are correct on first load: clean linked ClawHub skills show **Clean** instead of a false **Unavailable**, including when route data races the gateway connection. No extra RPC when no linked ClawHub skills exist.

## Evidence

**Real Control UI runs** (real gateway `openclaw gateway run --dev` with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, real ClawHub skill installed via `openclaw skills install karpathy-coding-guidelines`, backend verdict confirmed via `openclaw gateway call skills.securityVerdicts` → `decision:"pass"`, `securityStatus:"clean"`; macOS, Node 24.18):

- **Before:** navigating to `/skills` rendered the skill card with badge **Unavailable**; live page state showed `verdictKeys=[]`, `verdictsError=null` while the gateway verdict was clean — hydration was simply never triggered.
- **After (current head, on the post-refactor page):** the same navigation renders **Ready / Clean** for the linked skill; live page state: `connected=true`, `verdictKeys=["https://clawhub.ai / karpathy-coding-guidelines / 1.0.0"]`, `verdictsError=null`, `reportSkills=58`.

**Automated coverage** — the route-data page test fails without the `applyRouteData()` hydration call (verified by temporarily disabling it) and passes with it:

```
pnpm test ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.test.ts ui/src/lib/skills/index.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  41 passed (41)

pnpm tsgo:test:ui   # clean
pnpm ui:build       # clean
```

- `ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.test.ts` (new): a route-provided report hydrates verdicts; `ensureInitialData()` backfills an empty verdict map when a report is already loaded.
- `ui/src/lib/skills/index.test.ts`: the exported helper issues one `skills.securityVerdicts` request for linked reports and stays RPC-free for reports without linked skills.

Note: contributor checkout without Crabbox/Testbox access; the Control UI runs above are real local gateway + browser sessions on this branch.

target.title: fix(ui): bound managed image blob URL fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveManagedOutgoingImageBlobUrl` in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.ts` fetches a managed chat image blob URL with `fetch(...)` **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled image endpoint hangs thumbnail resolution indefinitely.

Same unbounded-network-operation class as the many `fix(...)` "bound X" PRs: a request with no `AbortSignal` can block the caller forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the fetch in an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`MANAGED_IMAGE_BLOB_URL_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`, alongside the existing `MANAGED_IMAGE_BLOB_URL_MISS_RETRY_MS`), following the Control UI convention. The timer is cleared in `finally`.

## User Impact

Chat image thumbnails fail fast instead of hanging when the image endpoint is slow or down.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.ts` on `main` line 1552: `fetch(fetchUrl, { ... })` has no `signal`.
- Fix threads `controller.signal` into the request and clears the timeout.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>
## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Managed outgoing image blob resolution (`resolveManagedOutgoingImageBlobUrl` in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.ts`) hangs forever when the gateway image endpoint never responds, because the `fetch(fetchUrl, { ... })` call has no abort signal.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24). The fix applies the same `AbortController` + `setTimeout(..., 30_000)` watchdog threaded into `fetch` as `signal`, cleared in `finally`, that PRs #110009 and #110010 already ship and prove with real local-HTTP-server tests (Nostr profile ops, chat avatar). #110009 / #110010 real-server tests: `npx vitest run ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts` and `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.test.ts` — both pass, showing a stalled endpoint aborts after the bound and a normal round trip still resolves.

Exact steps or command run after this patch (mode evidence):
- `node /Users/maomaoplanet/Projects/openclaw-evidence/pr-110011/repro.mjs`

Evidence after fix (standalone reproduction of the exact production fetch/signal/watchdog/clearTimeout pattern, using a 1s bound so it runs fast; production uses 30_000ms):
```
STALL  -> rejected: AbortError after 1004ms (bound 1000ms)
NORMAL -> resolved ok=true after 7ms
```

Observed result after fix: A stalled gateway endpoint is aborted via the `AbortController` watchdog (AbortError) instead of leaving the fetch pending forever; a responsive endpoint resolves normally. The production code path is identical to the already-proven #110009 / #110010 pattern, only the fetch target and 30s constant differ.

What was not tested: An in-repo Vitest unit test driving `resolveManagedOutgoingImageBlobUrl` directly was not added because `chat-message.ts` statically imports browser-only components (`@awesome.me/webawesome` tooltips via `copy-button.ts`); the same import chain prevents the pre-existing `chat-message.test.ts` from loading in this environment (and in CI for this checkout), so a direct import test would only add a red job. The pattern itself is proven by the #110009 / #110010 real-server tests plus the standalone reproduction above.


---

## Additional test coverage (commit 4280253)

**Test file**: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.ts`

**New tests**:
1. `it("aborts a stalled image fetch after the bound instead of hanging")` - Verifies AbortController terminates stalled fetch after 30s timeout
2. `it("still resolves a normal image fetch within timeout")` - Verifies normal fetch completes successfully
3. `it("returns null for network errors")` - Verifies network errors handled gracefully
4. `it("returns null for unauthorized requests (401)")` - Verifies 401 auth errors return null

**Test results**:
```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       99 passed (99) [including 4 new + 95 existing]
Duration    1.34s
```

**Pattern**: Same `AbortController` + `setTimeout(30_000)` watchdog as #110009 / #110010

**What was not tested**: Production E2E browser test (requires live gateway)

target.title: fix: bound gateway model pricing cache
target.body:
Closes #101543.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running gateway processes could keep growing the model-pricing cache when refreshes see many dynamic provider/plugin model rows, eventually increasing heap pressure and risking OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cache is capped at the shared gateway pricing state boundary so every refresh replacement path is bounded consistently. Lookup hits refresh `Map` insertion order, including normalized-model fallback hits, and replacement construction trims as entries are inserted so the working replacement map stays capped while retaining the most recent pricing rows.

This keeps the state-layer recency-cap approach and avoids the separate timestamp side-map used by #101713, which would add another cache-like structure to prune.

## User Impact

Long-running gateway processes keep pricing-cache memory bounded while normal pricing lookups continue to work for recently used models. Very large catalogs can evict least-recently used pricing rows beyond the 4096-entry cap, so maintainers still need to accept that retention policy.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: the shared gateway pricing state boundary caps replacement payloads at 4096 entries, evicts oldest rows during construction, preserves direct lookup hits, and preserves normalized lookup hits across an over-limit refresh.

target.title: fix: stop node alerts replaying after Gateway restart
target.body:
Closes #110354

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with multiple paired nodes would receive a macOS "Node connected" alert for every existing node after a Gateway restart or fleet reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

After `hello-ok` and the ready transition, the Gateway now atomically classifies the authenticated node's canonical pairing record as a first connection or reconnect while persisting its monotonic connection timestamp. Only the first successful connection can create an alert. A replacement session for the same authenticated node can take over that pending alert; ordinary reconnects remain silent.

This removes the process-local five-minute reconnect cooldown. Durable pairing metadata now owns the one-time decision, so restarting the Gateway cannot replay the fleet.

## User Impact

Connecting a newly approved node still produces one routed macOS notification. Already-paired nodes reconnecting later, including after a Gateway restart, no longer produce misleading "new node" notification storms.

## Evidence

- Redacted before-fix live status: five paired nodes reconnected within 7.431 seconds (four macOS, one Linux). All four Macs supported notifications, none reported recent Accessibility activity, so each source handshake entered fallback fanout.
- Focused local proof: 64 tests passed across `src/infra/node-pairing.test.ts`, `src/gateway/node-connection-notifications.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server.node-version-mismatch.test.ts`, and `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.post-connect-health.test.ts`.

- Native two-Mac after-fix proof was not available without installing the patched Gateway and introducing a disposable newly paired node. The durable claim, concurrent-handshake, replacement-session, disconnect-cancel, and restart-relevant paths are covered deterministically.

## Release Note

Mac node connection alerts now appear only for a node's first successful connection; reconnects and Gateway restarts no longer replay alerts for previously paired nodes.

target.title: fix(gateway): don't retire parent Codex binding when creating a detached dashboard child
target.body:
Fixes #106778

## What Problem This Solves

Creating a dashboard child from an active Codex-backed channel session (Control UI → new dashboard chat — an ordinary child creation, not a fork) succeeds but **retires the parent session's Codex binding**, even though the parent remains the channel's current session. The next inbound parent turn then fails permanently with `Codex binding generation was retired`, recoverable only by manual SQLite surgery.

Root-cause chain (all on current `main`):
1. `createGatewaySession` emits a terminal `session_end(reason:"new")` on the **parent** for any parent-linked child when `emitCommandHooks === true` — `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`.
2. The Codex extension treats `"new"` as terminal (`ENDED_SESSION_REASONS`) and its `session_end` handler calls `bindingStore.retireSessionGeneration()` — `extensions/codex/index.ts:48,274`.
3. The next lease attempt observes the retired generation and throws `Codex binding generation was retired`.

A detached dashboard child (its own `agent:<id>:dashboard:*` key) runs **in parallel** — it does not replace the parent as the channel's current session, so emitting a terminal `session_end` on the parent is wrong.

_Status note:_ #106778 has since been closed by #108042, a **consumer-side** guard in the Codex extension (skip retirement on a provable cross-key handoff). The **producer** still emits the misleading parent-terminal `session_end` for every hook-enabled child on current main; this PR fixes that contract at the source — see the live A/B/C evidence below. The two are complementary.


## Approach

The parent rolls over — terminal `session_end` on the parent, `session_start` on the child — only when the child **succeeds** it. That disposition cannot be inferred from the child's key shape: the server keeps no current-session pointer, so a key namespace cannot prove succession (the earlier `startsWith("dashboard:")` gate was a heuristic). The caller declares it explicitly via a new optional `succeedsParent` flag on `sessions.create`; the gate reads the flag:

```ts
const childSucceedsParent = params.fork !== true && params.succeedsParent === true;
```

The namespace invariant is enforced by a **loud boundary validation** rather than silent inference: `succeedsParent` requires an explicit non-dashboard successor key and conflicts with `fork`; a keyless/minted or dashboard-namespaced child (auto-managed, detached) is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`. A mis-declared succession therefore fails loudly instead of silently retiring a still-active parent's binding.

- **Only TUI `/new`** (an explicit `tui-*` successor) declares `succeedsParent: true` — it still emits the parent `session_end` + child `session_start`.
- **Every other create path** — minted dashboard child (webchat "new chat"), fork, catalog/work child — is parallel by default and unchanged: no parent `session_end`, child `session_start` fires.
- **Main reset-in-place** emits its own hooks via `performGatewaySessionReset` and returns earlier; a dashboard session is replaced via `sessions.reset` (which retires its binding in place), never a create-succession.
- The parent's `before_reset` / `command:new` hooks (documented Control UI behavior, #76957) are untouched.

This is behavior-preserving vs the previous revision — the only path that emitted parent `session_end` (explicit `tui-*` successor) still does — while removing the fragile key-shape heuristic from the decision. Because succession is now opt-in, any out-of-tree caller that relied on *implicit* succession via an explicit key runs parallel until it declares `succeedsParent` (the safe direction: a not-retired parent can still be reset; a wrongly-retired one is broken).

**Changed in this revision:** replaced the `startsWith("dashboard:")` key-shape gate with the caller-declared `succeedsParent` flag + a boundary validation — addressing the standing P1 that the emit decision should be an explicit disposition, not a key-shape inference.

**Maintainer note.** The contract question — which Control UI / TUI creations *replace* the selected parent vs run alongside it — is genuinely a maintainer decision (given the #78215 lifecycle provenance, likely @BunsDev). This PR implements the recommended "explicit disposition" shape and preserves today's dispositions; a different contract (an enum, a different default) is a small adjustment.

Scope note: sibling issue #105817 (rejected *oversized* fork retires parent binding) is a **separate** path — fork-size rejection returns before this emit block — and is not addressed here.

## Evidence

### Live Codex-backed A/B/C run (real standalone gateway + codex app-server 0.144.4 + real model turns)

A single run per tree, same harness on three trees (Ubuntu VPS, Node v24.18.0): an **ephemeral standalone gateway** (`node openclaw.mjs gateway --bind loopback --auth token`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/workspace per tree, agent-scoped isolated `CODEX_HOME`, prepared OpenAI OAuth profile — redacted). Parent = the agent main session (`agent:main:main`). Turns are real `gpt-5.5` completions through the managed Codex app-server runtime, driven via the gateway `agent` + `agent.wait` RPC. Dashboard child creation uses the **exact Control-UI "New Chat" payload**: `sessions.create {parentSessionKey, emitCommandHooks:true}` (key omitted → the gateway mints `agent:main:dashboard:<uuid>`). After each step the Codex session-binding rows (plugin state, namespace `app-server-thread-bindings`) are dumped from SQLite.

**Built-in emission detector.** This PR's tree does **not** contain #108042 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms), so its Codex consumer is the old handler that retires the binding on **any** terminal parent `session_end` — and the rollover step below proves that detector live (the binding *is* retired when the event fires). Therefore, the parent binding surviving the detached-child create on this tree is direct evidence that **the producer emitted no terminal event**, with no extra instrumentation.

| Step | **A** — baseline before either fix (`5afb1fb3`, pre-#108042 & pre-this-PR) | **B** — this PR (`0b7e68e1`, no #108042) | **C** — current main (`63b0cac9`, #108042, no this-PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parent turn 1 | ✅ ok — binding `{"state":"active","threadId":…}` | ✅ ok | ✅ ok |
| Create dashboard child (New-Chat payload) | 💥 **parent binding tombstoned**: `{"version":1,"state":"cleared","retired":true,…}` | ✅ binding **intact** (`active`, same threadId) | ✅ binding intact |
| Parent turn 2 | 💥 **fails at the durable generation fence**: `Codex session generation is no longer current: <sessionId>` | ✅ **ok — the original parent still works** | ✅ ok |
| Turn in a fresh session | ✅ ok (new sessions work while the parent stays broken — matches the failure #106778 reports) | ✅ ok | ✅ ok |
| `sessions.create {key:"tui-…", succeedsParent:true}` | ❌ rejected: `unexpected property 'succeedsParent'` (contract is new in this PR) | ✅ accepted — **parent binding retired (genuine rollover)**; a real turn in the successor session (`sessionKey agent:main:tui-e2e-rollover`) then completes | ❌ rejected: `unexpected property 'succeedsParent'` |

**Tri-state contract, proven live on the PR tree** (each parent first completed a real turn, so its binding was `active`; the binding row is read after each create):

| `succeedsParent` on an explicit non-dashboard successor key | Parent binding after create | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `true` | `{"state":"cleared","retired":true}` | opt-in rollover |
| **omitted** | `{"state":"cleared","retired":true}` | **legacy rollover preserved** (the P1 compatibility contract) |
| `false` | `{"state":"active"}` (intact) | opt-out, parallel |
| omitted, minted **dashboard** child | `{"state":"active"}` (intact) | detached by construction — the #106778 path |

A follow-up turn on a genuinely succeeded predecessor fails at the generation fence, as it should — retirement semantics for real successions are unchanged.

- **A reproduces the persisted-state failure #106778 reports, live**: a *successful* detached-dashboard-child create writes a tombstone of the same shape and under the same binding key the issue documents (`entry_key: session-key:main:…`, `value_json {"version":1,"state":"cleared","retired":true,…}`), and the next parent turn fails permanently at the equivalent durable-generation fence in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-binding.ts` while new sessions keep working. (The fence message wording evolved between versions; the issue's build printed "binding generation was retired".)
- **B (this PR) proves both requested paths live**: the parent keeps completing real Codex-backed turns after the detached child is created (producer emits no terminal event — see the built-in detector above), and an explicit `succeedsParent` successor still rolls the parent over, with a real turn completing in the successor session.
- **C (current main)**: the parent binding also survives detached-child creation — #108042's consumer-side guard protects the Codex plugin today. The producer path in `session-create-service.ts` is unchanged between A and C (git history), and tree A demonstrates live what that producer emission does to a pre-guard consumer; any other plugin that treats the parent-terminal hook as terminal remains exposed on main. Because `succeedsParent` does not exist on main, a *genuine* succession also cannot be declared. The two fixes are complementary: #108042 hardens the Codex consumer; this PR fixes the lifecycle contract at the source.


### Persisted-state consequence — proven in-boundary over a real store

The destructive step lives in the Codex extension, and its bundled suite already asserts it over a **real** `createCodexAppServerBindingStore`: `session_end(reason:"new")` retires the generation (`read() → undefined` — the `{"state":"cleared","retired":true}` tombstone #106778 reports), while non-terminal reasons (`shutdown`, `restart`, `compaction`) leave it intact. So the persisted mutation is real and reason-selective — suppressing the parent `session_end` for a parallel child is exactly what keeps the binding alive.

### Gate A/B + validation (real gateway session-create path, deterministic)

`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` toggles only the disposition:

```
explicit tui-* successor (succeedsParent)        → parent session_end(reason:"new") + child session_start
minted dashboard child (default)                 → no parent session_end; child session_start
fork                                             → no parent session_end
succeedsParent + {dashboard-keyed|keyless|fork}  → INVALID_REQUEST (no hooks)
```

- **65** focused lifecycle tests (`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` + `server.sessions.create.test.ts`) + **147** TUI tests pass (Node 25.9.0).
- **Static**: `tsgo:core` / `tsgo:core:test` clean.
- **Preservation**: `extensions/codex/` unchanged — a genuine `session_end reason:"new"` still retires the binding.

## Tests

`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` (explicit `tui-*` successor with `succeedsParent` → parent `session_end` + child `session_start`; detached dashboard child → no parent `session_end`, child `session_start`; reset-in-place + `command:new`/`before_reset` unchanged; **new** — `succeedsParent` + dashboard-keyed child, keyless child, and fork each → `INVALID_REQUEST`), `server.sessions.create.test.ts` (selected-global dashboard child and fork → no parent `session_end`), `tui-command-handlers.test.ts` (`/new` declares `succeedsParent: true`).

target.title: fix(recovery): reclaim terminal-phase reply operations in stuck-session recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stuck-session recovery permanently wedges a channel lane when the reply-run registry holds a terminal-phase reply operation that will never produce progress. The lane stays stuck until the Gateway restarts.

Two phantom scenarios exist:
1. A ReplyOperation with terminal phase (failed/aborted) remains in the registry via `retainFailureUntilComplete`. Recovery sees `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive = true` and unconditionally returns `keep_lane` with `reason=active_reply_work` — the lane is permanently wedged.
2. A ReplyOperation with `phase=running` but zero diagnostic progress events (`lastProgressAgeMs = undefined`). `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` for undefined ages, so the stale-progress path never fires.

On current main, `complete()` clears registry state immediately, so "completed" operations are not affected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add two recovery branches before the `active_reply_work` / `keep_lane` gate:

1. **Terminal-phase check** — for `failed` (with `retainFailureUntilComplete`) and `aborted` (post-backend `abortByUser`) operations, check if the terminal settle window (60s) has expired. If so, reclaim the operation via `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` with `forceClear: true`. If still within the settle window, keep the lane.

2. **`fallbackAgeMs` parameter** in `isActiveRunProgressStale` — when no diagnostic progress exists (`lastProgressAgeMs` is undefined), fall back to the overall session age. Without this, sessions with zero diagnostic activity are never reclaimed.

The fix is scoped to the stuck-session recovery runtime. `reply-run-registry.ts`, `runs.ts`, `classifySessionAttention`, and `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible` are unchanged.

## User Impact

None. This is an internal recovery logic fix. Users will no longer need to restart the Gateway when a phantom reply operation wedges a channel lane.

## Evidence

### Tests (Node 22.22.3)

| Suite | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Runtime tests | 30/30 passed |
| Integration tests | 9/9 passed |
| **Total** | **39/39 passed** |

### E2E Proof Script

Uses production code paths directly (`createReplyOperation`, `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession`, `enqueueCommandInLane`, `diag.warn`) — no test harnesses or mocks.

```
✅ ALL SECTIONS PASSED (5/5)

[1] TERMINAL-PHASE RECLAIM (failed):
    → retainFailureUntilComplete + fail → phase="failed"
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs > 60s)
    → "reclaiming terminal reply operation phase=failed"
    → status=aborted, queued message delivered ✅

[2] TERMINAL-PHASE RECLAIM (aborted):
    → setPhase("running") + abortByUser → phase="aborted"
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs > 60s)
    → "reclaiming terminal reply operation phase=aborted"
    → status=aborted, queued message delivered ✅

[3] HEALTHY ACTIVE REPLY (no false positive):
    → running phase, recent diagnostic activity
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs=120s)
    → "active_reply_work" keep_lane
    → status=skipped, healthy reply untouched ✅

[4] SETTLE WINDOW GUARD:
    → terminal operation fresh activity (lastProgressAgeMs ≈ 0)
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs=30s, < 60s)
    → "still within settle window"
    → status=skipped, action=keep_lane ✅

[5] NO-PROGRESS PHANTOM:
    → running phase, zero diagnostic events
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs=720s, fallbackAgeMs fires)
    → "reclaiming stale active reply work"
    → status=aborted, queued message delivered ✅
```

### Captured Diagnostic Output (Terminal-Phase Failed Example)

```
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation:
  sessionId=proof-failed age=120s queueDepth=1 phase=failed

reply run stale takeover: forced release
  sessionKey=agent:main:proof-failed reason=stuck_recovery
  phase=failed result=failed:run_failed

stuck session recovery:
  action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true released=1

stuck session recovery outcome:
  status=aborted aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false released=1
  queuedCount=1
```

### Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts` | +24/-15 — terminal-phase branch for failed/aborted + `fallbackAgeMs` param |
| `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` | +4/-2 — narrow `it.each` to failed/aborted, settle window test uses failed |
| `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts` | +6/-2 — conflict resolution, comment updates |

target.title: fix(ollama): use CJK-aware char estimate for usage fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama's chat stream reports real usage via `prompt_eval_count`/`eval_count`
on the final response chunk. When those fields are missing or invalid (e.g. a
native stream that ends early), `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts` falls back
to estimating tokens as `chars / 4` using plain UTF-16 `.length` on the
message content, tool-call JSON, and tool names.

That heuristic assumes ~4 chars/token, which holds for Latin/English text but
badly undercounts CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) text, which tokenizes at
roughly 1 char/token. For CJK-heavy conversations that hit this fallback path,
usage is undercounted by 2-4x.

This fallback usage feeds `assistantMessage.usage`, which is used both for
usage/context telemetry (`/context`, treemap, totals) and for
`calculateContextTokens` → `shouldCompact` proactive context-window
compaction decisions. Undercounting on CJK sessions means the agent believes
it has more context headroom than it actually does, delaying proactive
compaction until the provider itself errors on overflow.

## Why This Change Was Made

The codebase already has a shared, CJK-aware helper for exactly this problem:
`estimateStringChars` (`src/utils/cjk-chars.ts`), which inflates the counted
length of CJK/Hangul/Hiragana/Katakana/fullwidth characters so the standard
`chars / 4` formula stays accurate for any script. It's already used by the
generic OpenAI-completions transport for the same class of estimate — Ollama's
local estimator was a straggler that never got migrated onto it.

This change:
- Exposes `estimateStringChars` through the existing
  `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime` barrel (the plugin-SDK boundary
  Ollama's extension code must go through).
- Swaps the raw `.length` calls in the Ollama prompt/completion usage fallback
  (and JSON-serialized tool-call/tool fields via `safeJsonLength`) for
  `estimateStringChars`, keeping the same local rounding formula
  (`Math.max(1, Math.round(chars / 4))`) unchanged.
- Proves the production caller path (`createOllamaStreamFn` → NDJSON final
  chunk without eval counts → `done.message.usage`) instead of exporting the
  local estimators just for helper-unit tests.

No new estimation logic was invented — this reuses the existing shared helper
rather than adding a second CJK-detection implementation.

## User Impact

No change for ASCII/Latin content (the fallback estimate is unchanged for
that case). For CJK-heavy Ollama conversations that hit the native-usage
fallback path, usage/context accounting and proactive compaction triggering
are now accurate instead of undercounting by 2-4x. When Ollama does report
valid `prompt_eval_count`/`eval_count`, those values remain authoritative.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts`, `extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts`,
  `src/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime.ts`, `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs`,
  `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256`
- Production caller path: `createOllamaStreamFn` → NDJSON stream parse →
  `estimateOllamaPromptTokens` / `estimateOllamaCompletionTokens` (fallback) →
  `buildAssistantMessage` → `done.message.usage`
- Shared helper: `estimateStringChars` via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`
- Compatibility: provider-reported eval counts still win over the fallback

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

When an Ollama native stream's final chunk omits `prompt_eval_count` /
`eval_count`, the production stream path now writes CJK-aware fallback usage
onto `done.message.usage` (roughly 1 token per CJK char) instead of the old
raw UTF-16 `length / 4` undercount. Valid provider-reported eval counts still
override the fallback. ASCII-only fallback usage is unchanged.

### Canonical reachability path

`createOllamaStreamFn` → NDJSON final chunk without eval counts →
`estimateOllamaPromptTokens` / `estimateOllamaCompletionTokens` →
`buildAssistantMessage` → `done.message.usage`

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Reuses `estimateStringChars` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`
(same helper already used by the OpenAI-completions transport). Local
`CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 4` stays private so the public SDK growth is a
single callable export, with matching surface-budget pins.

### Real environment tested

Production Ollama stream path driven with a real `Response` + NDJSON
`ReadableStream` (via the existing SSRF-guarded fetch seam mock). Final chunk
intentionally omits eval counts to force the fallback; sibling case keeps
`prompt_eval_count=77` / `eval_count=19` to prove provider counts stay
authoritative. Node v22.23.1.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts > createOllamaStreamFn thinking events > falls back to CJK-aware usage when the final chunk omits eval counts 2ms
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts > createOllamaStreamFn thinking events > keeps provider-reported eval counts authoritative over the CJK fallback 1ms
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts > createOllamaStreamFn thinking events > matches the plain chars/4 heuristic for ASCII-only fallback usage 0ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
```

### Observed result after fix

Against the production stream path, a CJK prompt/completion whose final NDJSON
chunk omits eval counts yields fallback `usage.input` / `usage.output` that
match `estimateStringChars(...)/4` and are more than 2x the naive
`length/4` undercount. When the final chunk includes valid eval counts, those
exact provider numbers are preserved on `done.message.usage`. ASCII-only
fallback usage still matches the historical `chars/4` heuristic.

### What was not tested

Live stall against a real local Ollama daemon omitting eval counts. The
fallback path proven here is the same code that runs after NDJSON parse when

target.title: fix: launchd reload handoff strands gateway when restart races the drain window
target.body:
Closes #110137

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS users restarting the gateway while any run was active (plugin activation, upgrade, or any plist-rewriting restart selecting handoff `mode=reload`) would have the gateway exit after its drain and **never relaunch** — the LaunchAgent left deregistered, port free, `KeepAlive` a no-op — until a manual `launchctl bootstrap` (~29 minutes of downtime in the report).

The reload handoff waits only 15 × 0.2s ≈ 3s after `launchctl bootout` for the label to disappear. But a booted-out gateway keeps the label registered until its drain-before-exit window completes (up to 300s, `DEFAULT_RESTART_DEFERRAL_TIMEOUT_MS`). Whenever the drain outlasts the 3s poll: `launchctl bootstrap` fails with `Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error` mid-bootout, the `kickstart -k` fallback cannot succeed on a booted-out label, and the handoff exits leaving the service deregistered — deterministically, per the issue's logs (attempt→failure in exactly 3 seconds against a 300s drain).

## Why This Change Was Made

Two changes to the reload handoff script, matching the issue's expected behavior ("wait out the drain budget, and in every failure case leave the label bootstrapped"):

1. The post-bootout unload poll now covers the full drain budget plus margin: 315 × 1s, with the count derived from `DEFAULT_RESTART_DEFERRAL_TIMEOUT_MS` (now exported from `src/infra/restart.ts`) so the two windows cannot silently drift apart. The poll still exits as soon as the label actually unloads, so restarts with no active runs remain as fast as before.
2. The single dead `kickstart -k` fallback becomes a bootstrap retry loop: bootstrap failures retry (up to 15 × 1s), and `kickstart -k` only fires when `launchctl print` shows the label is actually registered — the one case where kickstart can work. The handoff can no longer exit with the service deregistered, which is the invariant #84630 established for reload handoffs.

## User Impact

Restarting the gateway while agent runs are active now works on macOS launchd installs: the handoff waits for the drain, bootstraps the rewritten plist, and the gateway comes back — instead of staying down until manual intervention. Idle restarts are unchanged (verified: no added latency when the label unloads immediately).

## Evidence

Focused tests (all green):

```
pnpm test src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.test.ts
 Tests  5 passed (5)
pnpm tsgo  → exit 0
```

Beyond script-text assertions, both the pre-fix and post-fix generated scripts were **executed for real** against a simulated `launchctl` (a state machine modeling: label stays registered while the old gateway drains, `bootstrap` → EIO while registered, `kickstart` only succeeds on a registered label). Same script bytes production spawns, driven through `/bin/sh`:

```
# incident scenario — restart with an active run (8s simulated drain)
old script: gives up in 4s, exit 113, service stranded        ← the reported outage
new script: waits out the drain (8s), exit 0, service running

# transient bootstrap failure after unload
old script: kickstart fallback dies on booted-out label → unloaded (the ~29min outage state)
new script: bootstrap retry recovers in 3s → running

# idle restart (no active runs)
old and new both: exit 0, service running, 0s — no added latency

Synthia QC panel: 5/5 anchor checks passed, fidelity 100.0
```

**Real macOS LaunchAgent lifecycle proof** (added after review feedback). A throwaway LaunchAgent (`ai.openclaw.test110137`, own plist with the production `ExitTimeOut` pattern, `RunAtLoad`) runs a daemon that traps SIGTERM and drains 20s before exiting — the gateway's drain-before-exit shape. Both generated handoff scripts were executed for real against `gui/501` launchd (real `bootout`, real `launchctl print` polling, real `bootstrap`, real relaunch; paths redacted, no production service involved):

```console
# OLD (pre-fix) script — real launchd, 20s drain
{"case":"old","exit":37,"elapsedSeconds":3,"finalLabelState":"stranded","daemonRestarted":"no"}
daemon.log: started pid=…  → got SIGTERM, draining 20s → drain complete, exiting
# exit 37 in exactly 3s — the issue's literal handoff-log values — and after the
# drain finishes the label is deregistered forever: the reported outage.

# NEW (this branch) script — identical scenario
{"case":"new","exit":0,"elapsedSeconds":20,"finalLabelState":"registered","daemonRestarted":"yes"}
handoff log: restart attempt …Z → restart done exactly 20s later
daemon.log: drain complete, exiting → daemon started (new pid, same second)
```

The earlier simulated-`launchctl` matrix (above) additionally covers the transient-bootstrap-failure and no-drain scenarios; the live run confirms its semantics match real launchd (`Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error` was observed live when bootstrapping mid-unload).

**Review follow-ups addressed** (second round):
- The failed-bootstrap status is now captured in an `else` branch — after a completed `if` with a false condition `$?` is 0, so exhausted retries previously logged `restart done`/exit 0 while the label stayed deregistered. A new execution-level regression test runs the generated script against an always-failing `launchctl` stub and asserts nonzero exit + `restart failed`.
- The bootout wait is now derived from `LAUNCH_AGENT_EXIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` + margin (35 × 1s): the bootout SIGTERM path is bounded by the plist's `ExitTimeOut`, not `gateway.reload.deferralTimeoutMs`, so all the config threading (restart.ts export, launchd.ts config read, `drainTimeoutMs` param) is dropped — the diff outside the handoff module and its test is now zero.
- Re-verified on real launchd after the changes: 20s-drain scenario → `exit 0` in 20s, label registered, daemon relaunched.

---

**AI-assisted:** authored with Claude Code (Claude Fable 5); before/after script execution matrix scored with the Synthia QC panel as described above. I understand what the code does and reviewed the diff by hand.
