target.title: fix(acp): persist spawn label to target session store instead of requester store
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `/acp spawn <agent> --label <name>` creates an ACP session for a **different agent** than the requester (e.g. from `main` into `claude` or `codex`), the operator-supplied `--label` was silently lost. Follow-up commands that resolve sessions by label — `/focus <label>`, `/acp status <label>`, and `sessions.resolve` — would fail with "No session found with label".

The root cause is a **store-partition mismatch** in `persistSpawnedSessionLabel`:

- The session key is `agent:claude:acp:<uuid>` (owned by the target agent, e.g. `claude`)
- But the label was persisted to the requester's store (`commandParams.storePath` → `agents/main/sessions/`)
- The requester's store has no entry for `agent:claude:acp:…`, so the write is a silent no-op
- The spawned session's store (`agents/claude/sessions/`) never receives the label

Session key generation always uses the target agent id (`spawn.agentId`), so this affects every cross-agent `/acp spawn` flow.

Fixes #106136

## Why This Change Was Made

`persistSpawnedSessionLabel` now resolves the canonical store path from the **spawned session key** via `resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` (`src/acp/runtime/session-meta.ts:76`) instead of using the requester's `storePath`. The in-memory `sessionStore` is only mutated when both stores resolve to the same path (same-agent spawn).

`resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` was previously unexported and only used internally in `session-meta.ts`. This PR exports it so `lifecycle.ts` can reuse the same canonical store-resolution boundary already trusted by sibling ACP metadata operations (`upsertAcpSessionMeta`, `listAcpSessionEntries`, `readAcpSessionEntry`).

## User Impact

- **Before**: Cross-agent ACP spawn labels (`/acp spawn claude --label novel`) were silently dropped. `/focus novel` failed. Only full session keys (`/focus agent:claude:acp:<uuid>`) worked.
- **After**: Labels persist to the correct target store regardless of which agent issues the spawn. `/focus <label>` and `/acp status <label>` work as expected for cross-agent ACP sessions.
- Same-agent spawns are unaffected — the store path resolves to the same location and behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Unit tests**: `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp.test.ts` — **67/67 passed**
**Typecheck**: `pnpm check:test-types` — passed
**Build**: `pnpm build` — passed

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Cross-agent ACP spawn label persistence — label written to target agent's session store, resolved via `sessions.resolve` by label.

Real environment tested: Linux x86_64 (kernel 4.19.112-2.el8), Node v24.15.0, branch `fix/acp-spawn-label-106136`, binary `OpenClaw 2026.7.2`.

**Gateway** — started with acpx lazy backend, 12 plugins loaded:

```
$ OPENCLAW_SKIP_ACPX_RUNTIME_PROBE=1 node dist/index.js gateway --port 18789
http server listening (12 plugins: acpx, anthropic, browser, canvas, codex, device-pair,
  file-transfer, memory-core, memory-wiki, minimax, phone-control, talk-voice; 3.4s)
gateway ready
```

**Cross-agent spawn** — `/acp spawn claude --label proof-1784006976795` via Gateway WebSocket `chat.send` RPC, requester `main_assistant`, target `claude` (acpx backend):

```
>>> {"type":"req","method":"chat.send","params":{"sessionKey":"agent:main_assistant:main",
     "message":"/acp spawn claude --label proof-1784006976795",...}}
<<< {"runId":"proof-spawn-...","status":"started"}

[event] chat reply:
  ✅ Spawned ACP session agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3
  (persistent, backend acpx).
```

**Label resolution** — `sessions.resolve` by label via Gateway WebSocket:

```
>>> {"type":"req","method":"sessions.resolve","params":{"label":"proof-1784006976795"}}
<<< {"ok":true,"key":"agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3"}
```

**Session list confirmation** — cross-agent session appears in list with correct label:

```
agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3 → label="proof-1784006976795"
# Owner is "claude" — cross-agent confirmed ✓
```

Observed result after fix:
- `/acp spawn claude --label` → session created as `agent:claude:acp:…` in target (claude) store ✓
- `sessions.resolve({label})` → returns `agent:claude:acp:…` (cross-agent owner) ✓
- Before fix: label was written to `main_assistant` store → silently lost ✗

target.title: fix(browser): cap fields-file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser CLI action commands accept `--fields-file` for form field descriptors. The previous reader loaded the whole file into memory before validating or parsing it, so a very large fields file could be fully buffered before the CLI rejected it.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a narrow 1 MiB byte cap to the `--fields-file` path only. The reader consumes at most the cap plus one sentinel byte, rejects oversized files before JSON parsing, and leaves inline `--fields` behavior unchanged.

## User Impact

Users get a friendly size-limit error for oversized Browser CLI fields files instead of the CLI buffering arbitrarily large input. Existing valid fields files and inline JSON fields continue to work.

## Evidence

Current head: `f1e87daf39c19b94e3a98d7074ac24e563615bd9`.

- Real behavior proof: `node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs --input-type=module <inline proof script>` imported `readFields`, parsed a valid fields file as `{ ref: "proof-ref", type: "text", value: "from file" }`, rejected a 1,048,577-byte fields file with `fields file exceeds 1048576 bytes`, and confirmed the oversized file was not parsed before rejection (`oversizedParsedBeforeReject: false`).
- Focused test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/shared.test.ts` passed 1 file / 8 tests.
- Formatting and whitespace: `node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.CMD --check extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/shared.ts extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/shared.test.ts` passed; `git diff --check -- extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/shared.ts extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/shared.test.ts` passed.

target.title: fix(i18n): sync Apple catalog with the Linux CI runner
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a broken-main condition where `apple-app-i18n` fails on the Linux CI runner for every PR: "Apple catalog apps/ios/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings is stale; run apple-app-i18n.ts sync-ios --write." This reddens `ci-gate`, blocking all PRs from landing even though the failure is unrelated to their changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The committed catalog was last regenerated on macOS. macOS's case-insensitive filesystem misses a source string that the Linux runner discovers ("Show reasoning & tool activity"), so `apple-app-i18n check` reports the catalog stale on Linux (iosKeys=1439 on Linux vs 1430 on macOS). CI truth is Linux Node 24, so the fix is to regenerate the catalog and the translation-contradictions report on Linux and commit the runner-matching output. Regenerated on a Blacksmith Testbox; `apple-app-i18n check` passes there after the write.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change — this is generated i18n metadata. Unblocks the shared CI gate so PRs can land again.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on a Linux Blacksmith Testbox: `sync-ios --write` then `check` passes (exit 0); only `apps/ios/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` and `apps/.i18n/apple-translation-contradictions.json` change.
- The added catalog entry is a real, fully-translated source string ("Show reasoning & tool activity") that the Linux scan finds and the macOS scan missed.
- Diff scope: +136 / -32 across the two generated artifacts only.

target.title: fix(mattermost): preserve websocket posts across restarts
target.body:
Related: #109657

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users could lose a posted message when OpenClaw received its WebSocket frame but restarted before the turn was adopted. Posted events were scheduled detached from the socket and protected only by a five-minute in-memory replay guard; reconnecting to Mattermost does not replay those already-received posts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost plugin now appends each raw `posted` envelope durably before handler scheduling, using `post.id` as the event identity and `channel_id` as the serialization lane. The shared core ingress drain owns recovery, per-lane ordering, bounded retry/dead-letter behavior, deferred debounce claims, and merged-turn adoption fan-out. The old replay guard is removed after its key-space parity is covered by 30-day/20,000-entry completion tombstones; `post_edited` remains outside this path so it cannot tombstone a later `posted` event.

Admission is serialized so an append retry cannot invert same-channel order. Transient append failures retry briefly; persistent failures terminate the WebSocket loudly instead of silently discarding later posts. Shutdown waits for in-flight admission and closes the prune/pump race.

Cold-gap limitation: Mattermost does not replay posts missed while OpenClaw is disconnected. This change protects frames OpenClaw received and durably admitted; it does not fill that platform-level gap.

## User Impact

Mattermost posts accepted by OpenClaw now survive process restarts and are dispatched once after recovery. target.title: fix(ollama): dripping model pulls hang past idle timeout during setup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenClaw Ollama setup could hang forever while downloading a model when `/api/pull` kept sending occasional NDJSON progress lines that never advanced `completed`.

Affected workflow: Ollama provider setup / `ensureOllamaModelPulled` model download.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ollama setup already aborts if headers never arrive (30s) and already fails if the pull stream goes fully idle (300s). After headers return, that response timer was cleared, so only the per-chunk idle timer remained. Idle resets on every chunk, so a slow drip can keep the download alive indefinitely.

This keeps the headers and byte-idle budgets as-is, then arms a **no-progress watchdog** after the first body chunk. The watchdog resets when aggregate Ollama `completed` increases **or when a never-before-seen status text appears**, so:
- non-advancing drips fail closed
- advancing large/slow downloads may continue past any fixed wall-clock lifetime
- healthy post-download finalization phases (first-time "verifying sha256 digest", "writing manifest", etc.) are not aborted
- cycling status values without completed progress cannot act as an unlimited keepalive

Optional `streamNoProgressTimeoutMs` / `streamIdleTimeoutMs` on `ensureOllamaModelPulled` are for tests only.

## User Impact

During Ollama setup, a wedged or maliciously dripping /api/pull stream fails closed with a no-progress error. Healthy pulls that keep advancing completed or transition through documented status-only finalization survive. True idle stalls still fail at 300s. Cycling status without completed progress is bounded.

## Evidence

Exact head: `0ffcb1caa29`

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull.test.ts extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

Coverage:
- existing idle-stall regression (empty body; no-progress not armed)
- fake-timer non-advancing drip fails with no-progress message
- fake-timer advancing completed continues past several shortened no-progress windows
- **NEW** fake-timer status-only finalization (distinct phases) survives past shortened watchdog
- **NEW** fake-timer cycling status without completed progress aborts within watchdog budget
- loopback negative idle control: drip + idle stays unsettled
- loopback non-advancing control: rejects with no-progress
- **NEW** loopback status-only finalization survives past 100ms budget
- **NEW** loopback cycling status aborts within 250ms budget

target.title: fix(ci): persist warm runtime caches across runs
target.body:
Related: #110298

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where CI cache writers reported successful Blacksmith sticky-disk commits, but later jobs repeatedly restored the original dependency, Vitest transform, and Node compile snapshots. The dependency store therefore repeated a 12.6 GB prune, and identical Vitest generations were cleared on every run instead of producing warm-cache gains.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime transform and compile caches now use immutable upstream Actions cache archives, which Blacksmith transparently accelerates. CI shards are restore-only; the daily or explicitly dispatched warmer is the sole test-cache writer, while build compile archives rotate at most once per UTC day.

The multi-GiB dependency tree remains on one O(1) sticky-disk family. Canonical main preflight is its sole serialized writer and 8 GiB maintenance owner, the key rotates from v4 to v5, and every consumer keeps the exact fingerprint fallback because [upstream stickydisk issue #54](https://github.com/useblacksmith/stickydisk/issues/54) documents delayed snapshot visibility even between dependent jobs. The stickydisk action pin also includes upstream's hot-attach zero-size fix.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Pull requests and main CI can restore warm transform and bytecode seeds without concurrent filesystem writers or per-PR sticky-disk growth. Old immutable Actions archives are bounded by normal LRU and inactivity eviction; only one live dependency sticky family remains.

## Evidence

- Before: dependency writer runs 29626241027 and later repeatedly committed fingerprint 75197f, but subsequent eu-west/X64 mounts still restored 73f052. Warmer 29627216071 pruned 69,431 files / 12.6 GB / 1,417 packages; later warmers repeated the identical prune.
- Before: identical Vitest generation f0d7e5 was cleared on every sampled run from 02:08 through 02:47 despite successful approximately 325 MB commit logs.
- Upstream contract checked: useblacksmith/stickydisk issue #54; PR #58 documents read-only parallel clones; commit 6d373c96 fixes hot-attach zero-size formatting races. Upstream useblacksmith/cache recommends the maintained actions/cache action because Blacksmith accelerates it transparently.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` — 82 passed, 1 platform skip.
- `node scripts/check-workflows.mjs` — zizmor and composite interpolation guards passed.
- `node scripts/docs-list.js` — passed.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Fresh branch autoreview — no accepted/actionable findings.

Post-land proof will dispatch the warmer once, verify a later Actions cache restore, verify a later main run restores the v5 dependency fingerprint, then delete only the four exact retired eu-west/amd64 v4/v2 identities.

target.title: fix(ollama): use CJK-aware char estimate for usage fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama's chat stream reports real usage via `prompt_eval_count`/`eval_count`
on the final response chunk. When those fields are missing or invalid (e.g. a
native stream that ends early), `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts` falls back
to estimating tokens as `chars / 4` using plain UTF-16 `.length` on the
message content, tool-call JSON, and tool names.

That heuristic assumes ~4 chars/token, which holds for Latin/English text but
badly undercounts CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) text, which tokenizes at
roughly 1 char/token. For CJK-heavy conversations that hit this fallback path,
usage is undercounted by 2-4x.

This fallback usage feeds `assistantMessage.usage`, which is used both for
usage/context telemetry (`/context`, treemap, totals) and for
`calculateContextTokens` → `shouldCompact` proactive context-window
compaction decisions. Undercounting on CJK sessions means the agent believes
it has more context headroom than it actually does, delaying proactive
compaction until the provider itself errors on overflow.

## Why This Change Was Made

The codebase already has a shared, CJK-aware helper for exactly this problem:
`estimateStringChars` (`src/utils/cjk-chars.ts`), which inflates the counted
length of CJK/Hangul/Hiragana/Katakana/fullwidth characters so the standard
`chars / 4` formula stays accurate for any script. It's already used by the
generic OpenAI-completions transport for the same class of estimate — Ollama's
local estimator was a straggler that never got migrated onto it.

This change:
- Exposes `estimateStringChars` through the existing
  `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime` barrel (the plugin-SDK boundary
  Ollama's extension code must go through).
- Swaps the raw `.length` calls in the Ollama prompt/completion usage fallback
  (and JSON-serialized tool-call/tool fields via `safeJsonLength`) for
  `estimateStringChars`, keeping the same local rounding formula
  (`Math.max(1, Math.round(chars / 4))`) unchanged.
- Proves the production caller path (`createOllamaStreamFn` → NDJSON final
  chunk without eval counts → `done.message.usage`) instead of exporting the
  local estimators just for helper-unit tests.

No new estimation logic was invented — this reuses the existing shared helper
rather than adding a second CJK-detection implementation.

## User Impact

No change for ASCII/Latin content (the fallback estimate is unchanged for
that case). For CJK-heavy Ollama conversations that hit the native-usage
fallback path, usage/context accounting and proactive compaction triggering
are now accurate instead of undercounting by 2-4x. When Ollama does report
valid `prompt_eval_count`/`eval_count`, those values remain authoritative.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts`, `extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts`,
  `src/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime.ts`, `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs`,
  `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256`
- Production caller path: `createOllamaStreamFn` → NDJSON stream parse →
  `estimateOllamaPromptTokens` / `estimateOllamaCompletionTokens` (fallback) →
  `buildAssistantMessage` → `done.message.usage`
- Shared helper: `estimateStringChars` via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`
- Compatibility: provider-reported eval counts still win over the fallback

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

When an Ollama native stream's final chunk omits `prompt_eval_count` /
`eval_count`, the production stream path now writes CJK-aware fallback usage
onto `done.message.usage` (roughly 1 token per CJK char) instead of the old
raw UTF-16 `length / 4` undercount. Valid provider-reported eval counts still
override the fallback. ASCII-only fallback usage is unchanged.

### Canonical reachability path

`createOllamaStreamFn` → NDJSON final chunk without eval counts →
`estimateOllamaPromptTokens` / `estimateOllamaCompletionTokens` →
`buildAssistantMessage` → `done.message.usage`

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Reuses `estimateStringChars` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`
(same helper already used by the OpenAI-completions transport). Local
`CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 4` stays private so the public SDK growth is a
single callable export, with matching surface-budget pins.

### Real environment tested

Production Ollama stream path driven with a real `Response` + NDJSON
`ReadableStream` (via the existing SSRF-guarded fetch seam mock). Final chunk
intentionally omits eval counts to force the fallback; sibling case keeps
`prompt_eval_count=77` / `eval_count=19` to prove provider counts stay
authoritative. Node v22.23.1.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts > createOllamaStreamFn thinking events > falls back to CJK-aware usage when the final chunk omits eval counts 2ms
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts > createOllamaStreamFn thinking events > keeps provider-reported eval counts authoritative over the CJK fallback 1ms
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts > createOllamaStreamFn thinking events > matches the plain chars/4 heuristic for ASCII-only fallback usage 0ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
```

### Observed result after fix

Against the production stream path, a CJK prompt/completion whose final NDJSON
chunk omits eval counts yields fallback `usage.input` / `usage.output` that
match `estimateStringChars(...)/4` and are more than 2x the naive
`length/4` undercount. When the final chunk includes valid eval counts, those
exact provider numbers are preserved on `done.message.usage`. ASCII-only
fallback usage still matches the historical `chars/4` heuristic.

### What was not tested

Live stall against a real local Ollama daemon omitting eval counts. The
fallback path proven here is the same code that runs after NDJSON parse when
those fields are absent or invalid.

### Fix classification

bugfix — usage accounting / CJK undercount

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the narrowed SDK export (only `estimateStringChars`),
caller-path proof, surface-budget pin, and CI knip unused-export fix.

target.title: fix(gateway): don't retire parent Codex binding when creating a detached dashboard child
target.body:
Fixes #106778

## What Problem This Solves

Creating a dashboard child from an active Codex-backed channel session (Control UI → new dashboard chat — an ordinary child creation, not a fork) succeeds but **retires the parent session's Codex binding**, even though the parent remains the channel's current session. The next inbound parent turn then fails permanently with `Codex binding generation was retired`, recoverable only by manual SQLite surgery.

Root-cause chain (all on current `main`):
1. `createGatewaySession` emits a terminal `session_end(reason:"new")` on the **parent** for any parent-linked child when `emitCommandHooks === true` — `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`.
2. The Codex extension treats `"new"` as terminal (`ENDED_SESSION_REASONS`) and its `session_end` handler calls `bindingStore.retireSessionGeneration()` — `extensions/codex/index.ts:48,274`.
3. The next lease attempt observes the retired generation and throws `Codex binding generation was retired`.

A detached dashboard child (its own `agent:<id>:dashboard:*` key) runs **in parallel** — it does not replace the parent as the channel's current session, so emitting a terminal `session_end` on the parent is wrong.

_Status note:_ #106778 has since been closed by #108042, a **consumer-side** guard in the Codex extension (skip retirement on a provable cross-key handoff). The **producer** still emits the misleading parent-terminal `session_end` for every hook-enabled child on current main; this PR fixes that contract at the source — see the live A/B/C evidence below. The two are complementary.


## Approach

The parent rolls over — terminal `session_end` on the parent, `session_start` on the child — only when the child **succeeds** it. That disposition cannot be inferred from the child's key shape: the server keeps no current-session pointer, so a key namespace cannot prove succession (the earlier `startsWith("dashboard:")` gate was a heuristic). The caller declares it explicitly via a new optional `succeedsParent` flag on `sessions.create`; the gate reads the flag:

```ts
const childSucceedsParent = params.fork !== true && params.succeedsParent === true;
```

The namespace invariant is enforced by a **loud boundary validation** rather than silent inference: `succeedsParent` requires an explicit non-dashboard successor key and conflicts with `fork`; a keyless/minted or dashboard-namespaced child (auto-managed, detached) is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`. A mis-declared succession therefore fails loudly instead of silently retiring a still-active parent's binding.

- **Only TUI `/new`** (an explicit `tui-*` successor) declares `succeedsParent: true` — it still emits the parent `session_end` + child `session_start`.
- **Every other create path** — minted dashboard child (webchat "new chat"), fork, catalog/work child — is parallel by default and unchanged: no parent `session_end`, child `session_start` fires.
- **Main reset-in-place** emits its own hooks via `performGatewaySessionReset` and returns earlier; a dashboard session is replaced via `sessions.reset` (which retires its binding in place), never a create-succession.
- The parent's `before_reset` / `command:new` hooks (documented Control UI behavior, #76957) are untouched.

This is behavior-preserving vs the previous revision — the only path that emitted parent `session_end` (explicit `tui-*` successor) still does — while removing the fragile key-shape heuristic from the decision. Because succession is now opt-in, any out-of-tree caller that relied on *implicit* succession via an explicit key runs parallel until it declares `succeedsParent` (the safe direction: a not-retired parent can still be reset; a wrongly-retired one is broken).

**Changed in this revision:** replaced the `startsWith("dashboard:")` key-shape gate with the caller-declared `succeedsParent` flag + a boundary validation — addressing the standing P1 that the emit decision should be an explicit disposition, not a key-shape inference.

**Maintainer note.** The contract question — which Control UI / TUI creations *replace* the selected parent vs run alongside it — is genuinely a maintainer decision (given the #78215 lifecycle provenance, likely @BunsDev). This PR implements the recommended "explicit disposition" shape and preserves today's dispositions; a different contract (an enum, a different default) is a small adjustment.

Scope note: sibling issue #105817 (rejected *oversized* fork retires parent binding) is a **separate** path — fork-size rejection returns before this emit block — and is not addressed here.

## Evidence

### Live Codex-backed A/B/C run (real standalone gateway + codex app-server 0.144.4 + real model turns)

A single run per tree, same harness on three trees (Ubuntu VPS, Node v24.18.0): an **ephemeral standalone gateway** (`node openclaw.mjs gateway --bind loopback --auth token`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/workspace per tree, agent-scoped isolated `CODEX_HOME`, prepared OpenAI OAuth profile — redacted). Parent = the agent main session (`agent:main:main`). Turns are real `gpt-5.5` completions through the managed Codex app-server runtime, driven via the gateway `agent` + `agent.wait` RPC. Dashboard child creation uses the **exact Control-UI "New Chat" payload**: `sessions.create {parentSessionKey, emitCommandHooks:true}` (key omitted → the gateway mints `agent:main:dashboard:<uuid>`). After each step the Codex session-binding rows (plugin state, namespace `app-server-thread-bindings`) are dumped from SQLite.

**Built-in emission detector.** This PR's tree does **not** contain #108042 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms), so its Codex consumer is the old handler that retires the binding on **any** terminal parent `session_end` — and the rollover step below proves that detector live (the binding *is* retired when the event fires). Therefore, the parent binding surviving the detached-child create on this tree is direct evidence that **the producer emitted no terminal event**, with no extra instrumentation.

| Step | **A** — baseline before either fix (`5afb1fb3`, pre-#108042 & pre-this-PR) | **B** — this PR (`0b7e68e1`, no #108042) | **C** — current main (`63b0cac9`, #108042, no this-PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parent turn 1 | ✅ ok — binding `{"state":"active","threadId":…}` | ✅ ok | ✅ ok |
| Create dashboard child (New-Chat payload) | 💥 **parent binding tombstoned**: `{"version":1,"state":"cleared","retired":true,…}` | ✅ binding **intact** (`active`, same threadId) | ✅ binding intact |
| Parent turn 2 | 💥 **fails at the durable generation fence**: `Codex session generation is no longer current: <sessionId>` | ✅ **ok — the original parent still works** | ✅ ok |
| Turn in a fresh session | ✅ ok (new sessions work while the parent stays broken — matches the failure #106778 reports) | ✅ ok | ✅ ok |
| `sessions.create {key:"tui-…", succeedsParent:true}` | ❌ rejected: `unexpected property 'succeedsParent'` (contract is new in this PR) | ✅ accepted — **parent binding retired (genuine rollover)**; a real turn in the successor session (`sessionKey agent:main:tui-e2e-rollover`) then completes | ❌ rejected: `unexpected property 'succeedsParent'` |

**Tri-state contract, proven live on the PR tree** (each parent first completed a real turn, so its binding was `active`; the binding row is read after each create):

| `succeedsParent` on an explicit non-dashboard successor key | Parent binding after create | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `true` | `{"state":"cleared","retired":true}` | opt-in rollover |
| **omitted** | `{"state":"cleared","retired":true}` | **legacy rollover preserved** (the P1 compatibility contract) |
| `false` | `{"state":"active"}` (intact) | opt-out, parallel |
| omitted, minted **dashboard** child | `{"state":"active"}` (intact) | detached by construction — the #106778 path |

A follow-up turn on a genuinely succeeded predecessor fails at the generation fence, as it should — retirement semantics for real successions are unchanged.

- **A reproduces the persisted-state failure #106778 reports, live**: a *successful* detached-dashboard-child create writes a tombstone of the same shape and under the same binding key the issue documents (`entry_key: session-key:main:…`, `value_json {"version":1,"state":"cleared","retired":true,…}`), and the next parent turn fails permanently at the equivalent durable-generation fence in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-binding.ts` while new sessions keep working. (The fence message wording evolved between versions; the issue's build printed "binding generation was retired".)
- **B (this PR) proves both requested paths live**: the parent keeps completing real Codex-backed turns after the detached child is created (producer emits no terminal event — see the built-in detector above), and an explicit `succeedsParent` successor still rolls the parent over, with a real turn completing in the successor session.
- **C (current main)**: the parent binding also survives detached-child creation — #108042's consumer-side guard protects the Codex plugin today. The producer path in `session-create-service.ts` is unchanged between A and C (git history), and tree A demonstrates live what that producer emission does to a pre-guard consumer; any other plugin that treats the parent-terminal hook as terminal remains exposed on main. Because `succeedsParent` does not exist on main, a *genuine* succession also cannot be declared. The two fixes are complementary: #108042 hardens the Codex consumer; this PR fixes the lifecycle contract at the source.


### Persisted-state consequence — proven in-boundary over a real store

The destructive step lives in the Codex extension, and its bundled suite already asserts it over a **real** `createCodexAppServerBindingStore`: `session_end(reason:"new")` retires the generation (`read() → undefined` — the `{"state":"cleared","retired":true}` tombstone #106778 reports), while non-terminal reasons (`shutdown`, `restart`, `compaction`) leave it intact. So the persisted mutation is real and reason-selective — suppressing the parent `session_end` for a parallel child is exactly what keeps the binding alive.

### Gate A/B + validation (real gateway session-create path, deterministic)

`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` toggles only the disposition:

```
explicit tui-* successor (succeedsParent)        → parent session_end(reason:"new") + child session_start
minted dashboard child (default)                 → no parent session_end; child session_start
fork                                             → no parent session_end
succeedsParent + {dashboard-keyed|keyless|fork}  → INVALID_REQUEST (no hooks)
```

- **65** focused lifecycle tests (`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` + `server.sessions.create.test.ts`) + **147** TUI tests pass (Node 25.9.0).
- **Static**: `tsgo:core` / `tsgo:core:test` clean.
- **Preservation**: `extensions/codex/` unchanged — a genuine `session_end reason:"new"` still retires the binding.

## Tests

`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` (explicit `tui-*` successor with `succeedsParent` → parent `session_end` + child `session_start`; detached dashboard child → no parent `session_end`, child `session_start`; reset-in-place + `command:new`/`before_reset` unchanged; **new** — `succeedsParent` + dashboard-keyed child, keyless child, and fork each → `INVALID_REQUEST`), `server.sessions.create.test.ts` (selected-global dashboard child and fork → no parent `session_end`), `tui-command-handlers.test.ts` (`/new` declares `succeedsParent: true`).

target.title: fix(recovery): reclaim terminal-phase reply operations in stuck-session recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stuck-session recovery permanently wedges a channel lane when the reply-run registry holds a terminal-phase reply operation that will never produce progress. The lane stays stuck until the Gateway restarts.

Two phantom scenarios exist:
1. A ReplyOperation with terminal phase (failed/aborted) remains in the registry via `retainFailureUntilComplete`. Recovery sees `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive = true` and unconditionally returns `keep_lane` with `reason=active_reply_work` — the lane is permanently wedged.
2. A ReplyOperation with `phase=running` but zero diagnostic progress events (`lastProgressAgeMs = undefined`). `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` for undefined ages, so the stale-progress path never fires.

On current main, `complete()` clears registry state immediately, so "completed" operations are not affected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add two recovery branches before the `active_reply_work` / `keep_lane` gate:

1. **Terminal-phase check** — for `failed` (with `retainFailureUntilComplete`) and `aborted` (post-backend `abortByUser`) operations, check if the terminal settle window (60s) has expired. If so, reclaim the operation via `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` with `forceClear: true`. If still within the settle window, keep the lane.

2. **`fallbackAgeMs` parameter** in `isActiveRunProgressStale` — when no diagnostic progress exists (`lastProgressAgeMs` is undefined), fall back to the overall session age. Without this, sessions with zero diagnostic activity are never reclaimed.

The fix is scoped to the stuck-session recovery runtime. `reply-run-registry.ts`, `runs.ts`, `classifySessionAttention`, and `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible` are unchanged.

## User Impact

None. This is an internal recovery logic fix. Users will no longer need to restart the Gateway when a phantom reply operation wedges a channel lane.

## Evidence

### Tests (Node 22.22.3)

| Suite | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Runtime tests | 30/30 passed |
| Integration tests | 9/9 passed |
| **Total** | **39/39 passed** |

### E2E Proof Script

Uses production code paths directly (`createReplyOperation`, `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession`, `enqueueCommandInLane`, `diag.warn`) — no test harnesses or mocks.

```
✅ ALL SECTIONS PASSED (5/5)

[1] TERMINAL-PHASE RECLAIM (failed):
    → retainFailureUntilComplete + fail → phase="failed"
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs > 60s)
    → "reclaiming terminal reply operation phase=failed"
    → status=aborted, queued message delivered ✅

[2] TERMINAL-PHASE RECLAIM (aborted):
    → setPhase("running") + abortByUser → phase="aborted"
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs > 60s)
    → "reclaiming terminal reply operation phase=aborted"
    → status=aborted, queued message delivered ✅

[3] HEALTHY ACTIVE REPLY (no false positive):
    → running phase, recent diagnostic activity
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs=120s)
    → "active_reply_work" keep_lane
    → status=skipped, healthy reply untouched ✅

[4] SETTLE WINDOW GUARD:
    → terminal operation fresh activity (lastProgressAgeMs ≈ 0)
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs=30s, < 60s)
    → "still within settle window"
    → status=skipped, action=keep_lane ✅

[5] NO-PROGRESS PHANTOM:
    → running phase, zero diagnostic events
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs=720s, fallbackAgeMs fires)
    → "reclaiming stale active reply work"
    → status=aborted, queued message delivered ✅
```

### Captured Diagnostic Output (Terminal-Phase Failed Example)

```
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation:
  sessionId=proof-failed age=120s queueDepth=1 phase=failed

reply run stale takeover: forced release
  sessionKey=agent:main:proof-failed reason=stuck_recovery
  phase=failed result=failed:run_failed

stuck session recovery:
  action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true released=1

stuck session recovery outcome:
  status=aborted aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false released=1
  queuedCount=1
```

### Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts` | +24/-15 — terminal-phase branch for failed/aborted + `fallbackAgeMs` param |
| `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` | +4/-2 — narrow `it.each` to failed/aborted, settle window test uses failed |
| `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts` | +6/-2 — conflict resolution, comment updates |

target.title: perf(sqlite): fast schema gates, background integrity verification, and downgrade protection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A user running a schema-11 agent DB (main/dev build) had the updater stop their healthy gateway and install v2026.7.2-beta.2, which supports schema 9. Every subsequent health/connect/message retry then ran a full synchronous `quick_check` + `integrity_check` + `foreign_key_check` over the 21 GB database on the gateway main thread (30-45s, 100% CPU), only to fail with "schema 11 > 9" - and nothing latched the failure, so the scan repeated forever. Three separate gaps stacked: the updater has no DB-schema preflight, the expensive integrity scan ran before the cheap version gate (#105179 ordering), and terminal open failures were retried from scratch.

Discussion context: Discord report by Dave Morin, sanity-checked against `main`; the integrity-on-open series (#104938, #105179, #105222, #106065, #108663) is a defensive response to the still-open corruption incident #101290 (broken `schema_meta` index).

## Why This Change Was Made

Downgrades must be refused instantly and cheaply at every layer, upgrades must stay proven and communicated, and full-file integrity scanning belongs off the hot path while keeping the detection #101290 still needs:

- **Cheap gates first**: both open paths now check `user_version` + schema owner before any scan. A newer-schema DB refuses in microseconds with an error naming the build that owns the DB (`schema_meta.app_version` is now stamped, previously always `null`) and linking the new docs page.
- **Scan rescoped**: steady-state opens verify only `integrity_check('schema_meta')` - the observed #101290/#105179 corruption class - plus the redundant `quick_check` pass is gone everywhere (`integrity_check` is a strict superset per sqlite.org/pragma.html). The full scan still runs where slow is correct: before a pending migration (now with a user-visible log line), in doctor/backup/compact, and in a new gateway background verifier.
- **Background verifier**: worker thread, first run 5 min after boot then daily, serial full `integrity_check` + `foreign_key_check` per DB, results persisted to a new additive `database_verifications` table in the state DB. On proven corruption it quarantines the DB: closes any live handle and latches the path so later opens fail fast until doctor repairs it.
- **Terminal-failure latch**: newer-schema and corruption failures latch per path (process-local); retries no longer rescan. Transient errors (BUSY, permissions) never latch. Doctor repair paths clear the latch.
- **Gateway boot preflight**: header-only version sweep of the state DB + registered agent DBs; refuses startup with one structured error per incompatible DB.
- **Updater preflight**: `package.json` now publishes `openclaw.schemaVersions`; `openclaw update` fetches the target's declared support (npm registry / git `show <rev>:package.json`) and refuses before stopping any service when an on-disk DB is newer than the target supports. Dry-run reports it; targets without metadata skip the check.
- **No new downgrade cliff**: deliberately no schema version bumps in this PR. The `database_verifications` table is additive derived cache (same fold pattern as 0c17cd4f1f2), so older builds still open the state DB.
- **Docs**: new `https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-schemas` - layout, versioning contract, per-version history mapped to release tags, integrity-check matrix, and an explicitly unsupported manual downgrade recipe with a worked 11->9 example.

## User Impact

- Beta upgraders from older releases: unchanged proven forward migrations (fixtures at schema 1/7/9/10 all land on current), now with a clear "migration pending, verifying integrity first" log instead of a silent multi-second stall on large DBs.
- Downgrade attempts: refused before the service is stopped (updater), at gateway boot (preflight), and at every open (version gate) - each refusal instant, actionable, and pointing at the docs page.
- Steady-state performance: per-open validation on a 756 MB DB drops from 763 ms to 1.6 ms (measured, ~475x); on the reported 21 GB DB that is ~30-45 s -> ~2 ms per open, and CLI one-shots stop paying a full-file scan per process launch.
- Corruption detection moves off-thread but stays daily and still fails closed before mutations via the schema_meta check, migration-time full scan, and quarantine latch.

## Evidence

- Focused suites (all green, single run): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-integrity.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-user-version.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-db.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts src/state/openclaw-database-maintenance.test.ts src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.test.ts src/state/openclaw-database-verify.test.ts src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.test.ts src/commands/doctor-state-sqlite-compact.test.ts src/commands/doctor.test.ts src/infra/update-check.test.ts src/infra/update-runner.test.ts src/cli/update-cli.test.ts src/infra/tsdown-config.test.ts test/release-check.test.ts src/gateway/server-startup.test.ts`
- Contract coverage: newer+corrupt DB fails with `SqliteSchemaVersionError` (no scan), latch fail-fast + clear-on-repair, quarantine closes a live handle, boot preflight fixtures, updater refusal before service stop (package + git modes, dry-run, missing-metadata skip), package.json/constants drift guard, worker bundle packaging guard.
- Perf: synthetic 756 MB agent DB - old per-open cost 763.2 ms (quick 171.4 + integrity 591.6 + fk 0.2) vs new 1.6 ms (schema_meta check 0.9 + version gate 0.7).
- `node scripts/generate-kysely-types.mjs --verify` clean; `git diff --check` clean; oxfmt clean on all changed files; docs MDX/link checks green (738 files, 6061 links).
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` (local fallback; Blacksmith backend timed out): all lanes green except the pre-existing main `check:test-types` orphans noted below; core `pnpm tsgo` clean, import cycles 0.
- Six structured autoreview rounds (Codex gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): every accepted finding fixed (durable quarantine rows enforced at open, preflight indeterminate fail-closed in the updater, post-stop TOCTOU recheck, git-metadata unreadable refusal, exact-version install pinning, doctor clear-failure surfacing). One consciously rejected finding remains, documented in code comments: when persisting a quarantine row fails (after a bounded retry of terminal rows), the quarantine stays process-local until the next daily verifier pass; the proposed durable out-of-band marker is a new storage surface (dedicated quarantine store) that needs a maintainer decision - flagged as follow-up.
- Post-rebase note: `check:test-types` is broken on current `origin/main` by two orphaned test files (`src/shared/deferred-event-buffer.test.ts`, `src/tools/protocol.test.ts`) whose prod modules were deleted by the deadcode refactors; unrelated to this PR and repaired separately on main.

target.title: fix(mxc): reject oversized sandbox policy files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators who configured an unexpectedly large file in `plugins.entries.mxc.config.mxcPolicyPaths` would have the entire file read and parsed synchronously when an MXC sandbox backend was created. A mistaken path to a large JSON file could therefore cause a large memory spike during gateway startup before the policy was rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

MXC now opens each sandbox policy once, checks and bounded-reads that same descriptor, and rejects files larger than 1 MiB before JSON parsing. The compatibility risk is that an unusually large but valid policy now fails closed; the documented upgrade path is to remove unnecessary whitespace or split it into multiple policy files, and boundary coverage verifies that a policy exactly at 1 MiB remains accepted.

## User Impact

MXC operators get an actionable error for oversized sandbox policy files instead of allowing an unbounded synchronous allocation during sandbox initialization.

## Evidence

**Real-machine production-path proof:** Linux `6.8.0-134-generic` x86_64, Node `v24.18.0`. The same harness directly imported the production `loadSandboxBaselinePolicy`, created a real 64 MiB JSON file on disk, invoked the loader, recorded process RSS, and then loaded a normal `{}` policy as a negative control. No filesystem or loader mocks were used.

**Before:** On pre-fix `upstream/main` at `d45e024dcabfd01abec24bf195fc2a6f0984cfef`, the production loader read and parsed all 64 MiB before schema validation rejected the extra field. RSS increased by 135,368,704 bytes and peak resident memory reached 223,332 KiB:

```text
{"sourceHead":"d45e024dcabfd01abec24bf195fc2a6f0984cfef","policyBytes":67108864,"oversizedError":"Failed to load sandbox policy file at <temp>/oversized-policy.json: Sandbox policy field <temp>/oversized-policy.json.padding is not supported.","rssBefore":92536832,"rssAfter":227905536,"rssDelta":135368704,"normalPolicyTimeoutSeconds":300}
Maximum resident set size (kbytes): 223332
```

Latest main at PR creation was `1aa0d73823a80e4674648328ff63bc162daed58e`; its loader blob is identical to the tested pre-fix source:

```text
d45e024dc:extensions/mxc/src/sandbox-policy-loader.ts  36cda6a4051482dd32c14e66b9764f46a1a222a8
1aa0d73823a:extensions/mxc/src/sandbox-policy-loader.ts  36cda6a4051482dd32c14e66b9764f46a1a222a8
```

Before this change, `readSandboxPolicyFile` passed each configured path directly to `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and then `JSON.parse`, so neither the existing `try/catch` nor schema validation bounded the allocation.

**After / negative control:** On commit `6bbe0ec8312e8786dfe1e786925e0b327db1409a`, the same production-path harness rejected the file from its 67,108,864-byte metadata before reading it. The size check and bounded read share one open descriptor, and the read loop independently enforces the cap if the opened file grows. RSS did not increase in this run, peak resident memory was 76,936 KiB, and the normal policy still loaded with the default 300-second timeout:

```bash

  /usr/bin/time -f 'max_rss_kb=%M elapsed=%e exit=%x' \
```

target.title: feat(feishu): route exact DMs with fail-closed enforcement
target.body:
Closes #110349

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where operators cannot bind one Feishu private conversation to a restricted agent without sender-scoped bindings also affecting the same sender in other conversations. For opt-in procurement-style workflows, an unmatched conversation, missing conversation ID, or unavailable target agent must stop before dispatch instead of reaching the main agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

This AI-assisted change adds exact literal `bindings[].match.conversationId` matching within the existing channel/account binding model and a Feishu-only `channels.feishu.dmRouteFailClosed` flag that defaults to `false` and follows existing account override behavior. The final DM gate runs after core routing, configured ACP overlays, and runtime ACP overlays; it does not add a global fallback switch, regex/fuzzy matching, a routing DSL, or changes to non-Feishu behavior.

## User Impact

Feishu operators can dedicate an exact private conversation to a restricted agent while keeping other conversations from the same sender isolated. When fail-closed mode is enabled, unmatched DMs, missing conversation IDs, missing agent targets, and plugin-owned runtime records without a core-routable agent are rejected before agent dispatch. Existing behavior remains unchanged when the flag is disabled.

target.title: fix(zalouser): settle waitForExit when abort signal already fired
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stopping a ZaloUser gateway account during or immediately after connection startup would leave `waitForExit` pending forever when the gateway stop `AbortSignal` was already aborted. Channel shutdown then waits on that race and never completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`monitorZalouserProvider` registered an `abort` listener without checking whether the signal had already fired; per the AbortSignal spec, listeners added to an already-aborted signal never run, so `settleSuccess()` is never called and `waitForExit` never resolves. The fix adds two guard points:

1. **Pre-try-block guard** (line 804): checks `abortSignal.aborted` before any async preflight work — catches signals already aborted at call time
2. **Post-preflight guard** (line 905): rechecks `stopped || abortSignal.aborted` after friends/groups resolution — catches signals that fired during the async preflight

Both guards match the pattern established in WhatsApp `connection-controller` (#109903), QQBot `gateway-connection` (#109896), and ZaloBot `monitorZaloProvider` (#109990).

## User Impact

ZaloUser channel stop/restart no longer hangs when shutdown is requested with an already-aborted stop signal (for example during fast gateway restarts or overlapping account lifecycle transitions).

## Evidence

### Layer 1: Platform-level proof (pure Node.js, zero dependencies)

A standalone Node.js script demonstrates the underlying AbortSignal specification behavior that makes this fix necessary. **No mocks, no vitest, no project dependencies** — runs with `node abort-signal-proof.mjs`.

```
============================================================
AbortSignal pre-aborted behavior proof
============================================================
Node version: v24.18.0

--- Test 1: Listener on pre-aborted signal ---
  signal.aborted = true
  abort listener fired = false
  VERDICT: PASS — listener never fires on pre-aborted signal

--- Test 2: Fix pattern (check signal.aborted before addEventListener) ---
  signal.aborted = true
  handled synchronously = true
  VERDICT: PASS — fix pattern catches pre-aborted signal

--- Test 3: Normal signal — listener fires on abort ---
  signal.aborted after abort() = true
  abort listener fired = true
  VERDICT: PASS — normal signal fires listener correctly

--- Test 4: Mid-flight abort (simulating preflight race) ---
  signal.aborted = true
  listener fired = true
  post-preflight recheck = aborted (post-preflight recheck catches this)
  VERDICT: PASS — both listener AND .aborted check work for mid-flight abort

============================================================
SUMMARY
============================================================
Test 1: Pre-aborted listener → NEVER fires        [SPEC BEHAVIOR]
Test 2: signal.aborted check → catches it         [FIX PATTERN]
Test 3: Normal abort → listener fires             [BASELINE]
Test 4: Mid-flight abort → both work              [POST-PREFLIGHT CHECK]
============================================================
```

### Layer 2: Production-function proof (real `monitorZalouserProvider`, only zalo-js boundary mocked)

A standalone vitest harness exercises the real `monitorZalouserProvider` function with a rich account config that triggers all resolution code paths (friends lookup, groups lookup, listener startup). The same harness produces different output on origin/main vs the fix branch.

**Before** (origin/main `b319493a529c` — function proceeds despite pre-aborted signal):

```
SCENARIO A: Pre-aborted signal
  signal.aborted = true
  elapsed: 2 ms
  listZaloFriends called: 1
  listZaloGroups called: 1
  startZaloListener called: 1
  total API calls: 3
  RESULT: ❌ FUNCTION PROCEEDED — 3 API calls made

SCENARIO B: Mid-preflight abort
  signal.aborted before abort() = false
  signal.aborted after abort() = true
  listZaloFriends called: 1
  listZaloGroups called: 1
  startZaloListener called: 1
  RESULT: ❌ GUARD MISSED — startZaloListener was called
```

On main, with a pre-aborted signal, the function:
- Calls `listZaloFriends` (API call to Zalo)
- Calls `listZaloGroups` (API call to Zalo)  
- Calls `startZaloListener` (starts Zalo session)
- For mid-preflight abort, `startZaloListener` is also called (no post-preflight guard exists)

**After** (fix branch `ffe5ebcfe2` — both guards work):

```
SCENARIO A: Pre-aborted signal
  signal.aborted = true
  elapsed: 1 ms
  listZaloFriends called: 0
  listZaloGroups called: 0
  startZaloListener called: 0
  total API calls: 0
  RESULT: ✅ EARLY RETURN — all API calls skipped

SCENARIO B: Mid-preflight abort
  signal.aborted before abort() = false
  signal.aborted after abort() = true
  listZaloFriends called: 1
  listZaloGroups called: 1
  startZaloListener called: 0
  RESULT: ✅ POST-PREFLIGHT GUARD — startZaloListener skipped
```

On the fix branch:
- **Guard 1** (pre-aborted): returns `{stop}` in 1ms, 0 API calls
- **Guard 2** (mid-preflight): friends/groups resolve, but `startZaloListener` is skipped because `stopped || abortSignal.aborted` is true

### Layer 3: Regression tests

All lifecycle tests pass on fix branch (24 tests across 2 files):

```
✓ returns before startZaloListener when the abort signal is already fired
✓ resolves mutable allowlist and group names at startup when enabled
```

### Proof harness sources

- **Layer 1**: standalone Node.js script (zero dependencies) — demonstrates AbortSignal spec behavior
- **Layer 2**: vitest harness importing real `monitorZalouserProvider` with zalo-js boundary mocked — demonstrates fix applied correctly
- **Layer 3**: committed regression tests in `monitor.account-scope.test.ts` and `monitor.group-gating.test.ts`

Run Layer 1 with: `node abort-signal-proof.mjs`
Run Layer 2 with: `npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-zalo.config.ts --reporter verbose`

## Diff

Source: +49 / -36 lines in `monitor.ts` (move lifecycle vars before try block + pre-aborted guard + post-preflight recheck).
Tests: +53 lines in `monitor.account-scope.test.ts` (pre-aborted regression test) + 8 lines in `monitor.group-gating.test.ts` (update test helper for new guard).

target.title: fix(doctor): warn when maxActiveTranscriptBytes is set without truncateAfterCompaction
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** `resolveMaxActiveTranscriptBytes()` returns `undefined` when `truncateAfterCompaction` is not `true`, even if `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` is configured with a positive value. The byte guard silently has no effect, but there is no diagnostic to warn the operator.
- **Root cause:** The function at `src/auto-reply/reply/memory-flush.ts:27-29` gates on `truncateAfterCompaction === true` before parsing `maxActiveTranscriptBytes`, returning `undefined` otherwise.
- **Solution:** Add a Doctor health check (`core/doctor/inactive-compaction-byte-guard`) that warns when `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` resolves to a positive effective byte limit but `truncateAfterCompaction` is not enabled. Uses `parseNonNegativeByteSize` to normalize values, so zero-value forms like `"0mb"`, `"0KB"`, and numeric `0` do NOT produce false-positive warnings.

Closes #100529

## What changed

- `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts` — added `collectCompactionByteGuardFindings` (uses `parseNonNegativeByteSize` for byte-size normalization), `runCompactionByteGuardHealth`, and a `doctor:compaction-byte-guard` contribution (opt-in, `defaultEnabled: false`)
- `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts` — 4 test cases: (1) warns for positive limit without truncation, (2) silent when truncation enabled, (3) silent when not configured, (4) silent for zero-value byte sizes (`0`, `"0"`, `"0mb"`, `"0MB"`, `"0kb"`, `"0gb"`, `"0b"`)

target.title: fix(memory-embeddings): use longer backoff for rate-limit (429) errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw memory index` encounters a rate-limit (429) error from the embedding provider, the retry loop uses the normal 500ms base delay with an 8000ms cap. Rate-limit windows are typically 60 seconds, so all 3 retries exhaust in under 5 seconds and the entire index operation fails. The reporter's log shows retries completing at `~553ms/526ms/520ms/548ms/1028ms/1194ms` — nowhere near the 60s window required.

## Changes

- **New `isRateLimitMemoryEmbeddingError()` in policy** — separately detects 429 / `resource has been exhausted` errors vs general transient errors (5xx, network blips)
- **`rateLimitBaseDelayMs` (30s) param on `runMemoryEmbeddingRetryLoop`** — when a rate-limit error fires, use this base instead of the normal `500ms`; produces wait sequence: 30s → 60s → 120s
- **`rateLimitMaxDelayMs` (120s) in `waitForEmbeddingRetry`** — used when the computed delay already exceeds the normal 8s cap, so the longer rate-limit delay isn't clamped away
- **Threaded through `runMemoryEmbeddingBatchRetryWithSplit`** — both retry loops and recursive split calls get the same longer backoff for rate-limit errors
- Normal transient errors (connection reset, fetch failed, timed out, 5xx) still use the original 500ms base — no regression

## Evidence

- All 18 existing tests pass (including the 3 new rate-limit backoff tests)
- New test `uses longer backoff for rate-limit errors when rateLimitBaseDelayMs is set` confirms: 429 error with default config produces waits = [30000, 60000] before exhausting 3 attempts
- New test `still uses short backoff for non-rate-limit retryable errors even when rateLimitBaseDelayMs is set` confirms: transient `fetch failed` with the same config still uses [500ms] delay — no cross-contamination
- The `waitForEmbeddingRetry` max-delay detection is implicit: if `delayMs > 8000` (the normal cap), the code picks the rate-limit cap; otherwise the normal 8s cap

target.title: fix(qa-lab): bound credential payload reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QA Lab credential add commands enforced `OPENCLAW_QA_CREDENTIAL_PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES` with a file stat before reading the payload. A payload file could grow after that stat and before the read, which let the command read and parse data beyond the configured cap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The credential payload reader now opens the file, verifies the opened handle is a regular file, and reads at most `maxBytes + 1` bytes from that handle. ## User Impact

Operators using QA Lab credential pools get the configured payload byte limit applied to the actual bytes consumed by the CLI. Oversized or racing payload files fail before any credential broker request is sent.

target.title: fix(gradium): return false from isConfigured on invalid baseUrl instead of throwing

## What Problem This Solves

The Gradium speech provider's `isConfigured` predicate throws when `providerConfig.baseUrl` is malformed or points to a non-Gradium host, instead of returning `false`. The predicate calls `readGradiumProviderConfig`, which normalizes `baseUrl` via `normalizeGradiumBaseUrl` — and that function throws on invalid input.

This means a misconfigured `baseUrl` (e.g., `https://example.com` or `not-a-url`) causes the provider check to crash rather than gracefully report the provider as unavailable.

Fixes #108550

## Fix

Wrap the `isConfigured` body in a try-catch that returns `false` on any error from `readGradiumProviderConfig`. The `synthesize` and `synthesizeTelephony` paths still throw on invalid URLs (correct behavior — they should not silently proceed with a bad endpoint).

## Evidence

```
→ throws: "Gradium baseUrl must target api.gradium.ai"
```

## What Problem This Solves

The Telegram Mini App auth endpoint (`/__openclaw_tg_miniapp/auth`) enforces only a 4 KiB body size limit with no read timeout. An unauthenticated client can send an incomplete body indefinitely, holding request-processing resources open at the ingress boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the manual chunk-by-chunk body buffer with the shared `readRequestBodyWithLimit` helper, reusing the existing `WEBHOOK_BODY_READ_DEFAULTS.preAuth.timeoutMs` timeout strategy:
- On timeout the SDK layer aborts the request and throws a `REQUEST_BODY_TIMEOUT` error.
- The route handler maps that error to an HTTP 408 response with `"Request body timeout"` — symmetric with the existing 413 `"Payload too large"` branch.

## User Impact

Unauthenticated slow-body attacks against the Mini App auth route are now bounded by the configured pre-auth timeout, releasing the request and connection instead of holding them open.

target.title: fix(elevenlabs): reject malformed base URL overrides
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a malformed or non-HTTP(S) ElevenLabs `baseUrl` in provider config is
either crashed on with an uncaught `TypeError: Invalid URL` or silently accepted, instead of
being rejected with an actionable error.

`normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` in `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.ts` only trimmed the value and
stripped trailing slashes — it never confirmed the result was a parseable HTTP(S) URL. Its
callers feed the result straight into `new URL(...)`: `normalizeElevenLabsRealtimeBaseUrl`
(`realtime-transcription-provider.ts:134`) does `new URL(normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl(value))`,
and TTS/speech/media-understanding consume the same helper.

**Concrete example:** with `baseUrl: "not a url"`, `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` on current `main`
returns `"not a url"` unchanged and the downstream `new URL("not a url")` throws an opaque
`TypeError: Invalid URL`. A value like `ftp://files.example.com` parses but is not a usable
ElevenLabs endpoint, yet is accepted and passed to fetch/WebSocket construction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate the base URL at the shared config boundary and **fail actionably**: only an absent/blank
value falls back to `DEFAULT_ELEVENLABS_BASE_URL`; an explicit value that is unparseable, or whose
scheme is not `http:`/`https:`, throws a clear `Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl` error. This mirrors the
merged `fix(microsoft-foundry): reject malformed endpoints` (#104796) precedent — reject malformed
explicit endpoints rather than silently retargeting them. An operator's explicit custom endpoint is
their intent, so it is never silently swapped for the default (which would change behavior across all
four consumers on upgrade); valid `http(s)` endpoints are trimmed/normalized exactly as before.

## User Impact

**Before:** a mistyped ElevenLabs `baseUrl` surfaces an opaque `TypeError: Invalid URL` at session
setup, and a non-HTTP(S) endpoint is accepted and produces unusable fetch/WebSocket URLs.

**After:** an explicit malformed or non-HTTP(S) `baseUrl` fails fast with an actionable error; absent/blank
config still defaults; valid custom `http(s)` endpoints are unchanged. Validation errors never echo the raw
configured URL, so embedded userinfo or credential-bearing query params are not disclosed to logs/diagnostics.

## Evidence

- `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.ts` — `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` rejects explicit malformed / non-HTTP(S) values (throws) and only defaults absent/blank input. Error messages are redacted: the malformed case says "value is not a valid URL"; the scheme case surfaces only the offending `protocol`, never the raw URL.
- Regression test: `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.test.ts` — asserts absent/blank → default, valid → normalized, explicit malformed → throws, `ftp:`/`data:` → throws `unsupported scheme`, and (disclosure test) a `baseUrl` with userinfo + `api_key` query is rejected **without** its secret/token appearing in the error. The malformed/scheme cases fail on the pre-fix `.trim()`-only version; the disclosure test fails on the earlier raw-value error and passes after redaction.
- Function probe against the real production `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl`:

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import('./extensions/elevenlabs/shared.ts').then(m => …)"
undefined -> "https://api.elevenlabs.io"
"https://custom.example.com/" -> "https://custom.example.com"
"not a url" -> THROWS: Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: value is not a valid URL
"ftp://user:sup3r-secret@files.example.com?api_key=leak-me" -> THROWS: Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: unsupported scheme "ftp:" (expected http or https)
```

(The credential-bearing input above is rejected with no `sup3r-secret` / `leak-me` / `api_key` in the message.)

target.title: fix(agents): reduce cron trigger script maxLength to 2000 for llama.cpp GBNF compatibility
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Llama.cpp GBNF grammar compiler enforces a hard repetition ceiling (~2000) when converting JSON Schema `maxLength` constraints to GBNF format. The cron tool `trigger.script` field had `maxLength: 65_536` in the LLM-facing tool parameter schema — this created a repetition up to 65,536 which exceeds the ceiling. The GBNF compilation failure causes every request to return 400 when the cron tool is present in active tools, on any channel.

Fixes #108580

## Why This Change Was Made

**Approach**: Instead of setting an artificial low `maxLength` (which could reject legitimate 2001–65536-character model-generated scripts), the LLM-facing tool parameter schema now **omits `maxLength` entirely** on `trigger.script`. GBNF compiles unbounded string fields with `[^]+` (one-or-more, no repetition limit), so this avoids the ceiling issue entirely.

Protocol-layer validation (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts`) still enforces `maxLength: 65536` server-side for direct RPC calls. Only the LLM-facing tool schema (compiled into GBNF grammar) was changed.

## User Impact

Users running llama.cpp (or any provider using GBNF grammar compilation) will no longer get 400 errors when the cron tool is enabled. Existing protocol-level limits for direct RPC scripts remain unchanged at 65536 bytes.

## How the fix avoids GBNF compilation failure

**Before (broken)**: The JSON Schema emitted to the LLM for `trigger.script` was:
```json
{"type": "string", "minLength": 1, "maxLength": 65536}
```
This compiles to GBNF `string ::= [^] (1-65536 times)` which exceeds llama.cpp internal repetition ceiling.

**After (fixed)**: The JSON Schema emitted to the LLM is now:
```json
{"type": "string", "minLength": 1}
```
This compiles to GBNF `string ::= [^]+` which is always valid. The schema is GBNF-compatible with no repetition constraint.

## Schema Contract Summary

| Layer | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| LLM-facing (`cron-tool.ts`) | `maxLength: 65536` → GBNF ❌ | no `maxLength` → GBNF `[^]+` ✅ |
| Protocol (`gateway-protocol/cron.ts`) | `maxLength: 65536` | `maxLength: 65536` (unchanged) |

Server-side RPC validation still rejects `trigger.script` values exceeding 65,536 characters. Only the LLM-facing tool schema (compiled to GBNF grammar) was relaxed.

## Evidence

### 1. Unit tests — all passing (including new GBNF-safe regression test)

A recursive test walks the full cron tool parameter schema and asserts no string field has a `maxLength` exceeding the GBNF-safe ceiling (~2000), preventing future regressions:

```
 ✓ cron tool > keeps trigger.script GBNF-safe (no maxLength that exceeds llama.cpp repetition ceiling)

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  322 passed (322)
   Duration  6.77s
```

### 2. Gateway startup — cron service enabled and healthy

```
[gateway] agent model: llama-cpp/llama-cpp-gbnf (thinking=off, fast=off)
[gateway] http server listening (13 plugins; 5.4s)
[gateway] ready
[cron]   cron: started {"enabled":true,"jobs":0}
```

### 3. Gateway API — cron CRUD operations verified

```bash
# cron.list — successful
⇄ res ✓ cron.list 8ms

# cron.add — successful, job created with full schema
{
  "id": "0b1f38ff-...",
  "name": "gbnf-verification",
  "enabled": true,
  "schedule": { "kind": "every", "everyMs": 3600000 },
  "payload": { "kind": "agentTurn", "message": "Verification test" }
}

# cron.remove — successful
{ "ok": true, "removed": true }
```

### 4. Protocol-level schema unchanged

`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` retains `maxLength: 65536` for the `trigger.script` field, validated server-side:
```typescript
export const CronTriggerSchema = closedObject({
  script: Type.String({ minLength: 1, maxLength: 65_536 }),
  once: Type.Optional(Type.Boolean()),
});
```

### 5. Code change (single line, well-commented)

```diff
- script: Type.String({ minLength: 1, maxLength: 65_536 }),
+ // No maxLength here: GBNF grammar compilers (llama.cpp) reject schemas
+ // with repetition ceilings above ~2000. Protocol-layer validation in
+ // packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts enforces maxLength:65536
+ // server-side for direct RPC calls.
+ script: Type.String({ minLength: 1 }),
```

## Files Changed

| File | Additions | Deletions | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` | +5 | −1 | Remove LLM-facing `maxLength` on `trigger.script` |
| `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts` | +34 | 0 | Recursive GBNF-safe regression test over full schema |

Total: +39 / −1 across 2 files.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw models auth paste-token` and `paste-api-key` accumulated piped stdin without any size limit, allowing arbitrarily large input to buffer in memory before reaching downstream validation.

target.title: feat(gateway): idempotent start, non-interactive stop guard, unified lifecycle audit
target.body:
## Summary

Agents (and scripts) have been fighting over operators' running gateways: `gateway start` on a loaded service silently restarted it, non-interactive `gateway stop` could bootout a production service or SIGTERM a dev gateway it never started, and `gateway run --force` killed whatever held the port. Most restarts also bypassed the `gateway-restart.log` audit trail.

## Changes

- `gateway start` is now idempotent: loaded + running -> "already running (pid N)", exit 0. No hidden restart.
- `gateway stop` in a non-interactive shell requires `--force`; the refusal teaches the isolated-dev-gateway path (`run --dev` / `--profile` + free port). Interactive behavior unchanged. Applies to managed bootout and the unmanaged port-SIGTERM fallback. The system-agent approval flow supplies `force` (its approval gate is the consent).
- `gateway run --force` in a non-interactive shell refuses to kill a verified existing gateway listener, with per-signal revalidation (no check-then-kill race); fuser fallback resolves and validates concrete PIDs (stdout only) before signaling.
- Unified lifecycle audit: every start/stop/restart mutation (cli, safe-rpc, supervisor, handoff) appends a key=value line to `gateway-restart.log`, immediately after each successful mutation, best-effort.

## Proof

- Focused suites green across daemon + CLI shards (service, lifecycle, launchd/systemd/schtasks, ports/run guards): 400+ tests.
- tsgo core + core:test green on Blacksmith Testbox.
- Structured review (Codex gpt-5.6-sol): two hardening rounds (fuser TOCTOU, stderr PID parsing, partial-mutation audit ordering) fixed; final run clean.

Docs: `docs/cli/gateway.md` updated. Policy context: AGENTS.md "Tests" live-gateway rules (2ca4d92f1ae).

target.title: fix(config): compaction.enabled field rejected by config schema despite being read by the runtime
target.body:
Closes #110065

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could not disable auto-compaction through configuration. The session runtime reads `compaction.enabled` to control auto-compaction on/off (`settings-manager.ts:667`: `this.settings.compaction?.enabled ?? true`), but the config schema's `.strict()` Zod object for compaction did not include `enabled`. Setting `enabled: false` in `openclaw.json` caused the entire config to be rejected as invalid with `agents.defaults.compaction: Invalid input`.

Users experiencing premature compaction had no `enabled: false` workaround while waiting for underlying usage-accounting fixes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `enabled: z.boolean().optional()` to the compaction Zod schema — matching the runtime's existing `?? true` default. The field is optional: absent means enabled (the existing default), `false` disables auto-compaction entirely as the settings manager intended. The schema stays `.strict()` so truly unknown fields are still rejected. A new schema help entry documents the field.

## User Impact

Users can now set `compaction.enabled: false` in `openclaw.json` (or via `openclaw config set`) to disable automatic context compaction. Absent configurations behave exactly as before (`enabled` defaults to true).

## Evidence

### Schema validation regression (real Zod config schema)

- `validateConfigObject({ agents: { defaults: { compaction: { enabled: false } } } })` — passes with the fix; fails against unfixed `main` (the `.strict()` schema rejects `enabled` as an unrecognized key).
- `validateConfigObject({ agents: { defaults: { compaction: { nonexistentField: true } } } })` — still fails in both states, proving the `.strict()` guard stays intact.

### Unit regression coverage

- `config.compaction-settings.test.ts`: 7 tests pass (2 new: compaction.enabled toggle accepted; absent defaults to undefined for runtime `?? true`).
- `config.schema-regressions.test.ts`: 38 tests pass (2 new, including the strictness-preservation test).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on both files passes.
- Scoped `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` pass on the four changed files.

target.title: fix(ui): bound chat avatar metadata and image fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`refreshChatAvatar` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.ts` issues two `fetch` calls — the avatar metadata lookup and the local avatar image download — **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled gateway leaves avatar resolution pending indefinitely, blocking the chat header update.

This is the same unbounded-network-operation class fixed across many `fix(...)` "bound X" PRs: a request with no `AbortSignal` can hang the caller forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`CHAT_AVATAR_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`) around both fetches, matching the Control UI convention used by `agent-select.ts` (`AGENT_SELECT_AVATAR_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`). The timer is cleared in `finally`.

## User Impact

Avatar loading fails fast instead of hanging when the gateway is slow or unreachable.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.ts` on `main`: both `fetch` calls have no `signal`.
- Fix threads `controller.signal` into both requests and clears the timeout.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>
## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Chat avatar resolution (`refreshChatAvatar` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.ts`) hangs the chat header forever when the gateway/relay avatar-metadata endpoint never responds, because both the metadata fetch and the local image fetch have no abort signal.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9, local HTTP server (`node:http`) bound to 127.0.0.1:0. Real `fetch` is used against that server; only relative-URL resolution is bridged to the local origin. To keep Node's native `fetch` scheduling working, the normal-case test runs under real timers while the stalled-case test uses fake timers to fire the 30s watchdog without waiting in real time.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.test.ts`

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
 - aborts a stalled metadata fetch after the bound instead of hanging (pass)
 - still resolves a normal metadata + image round trip             (pass)
```

Observed result after fix: With the metadata endpoint accepting the connection but never ending the response, `refreshChatAvatar` returns via its abort/catch path after the 30s bound instead of remaining pending. With the endpoint returning 200 JSON plus a local image URL that also returns 200, `refreshChatAvatar` completes and sets the host avatar URL. Ordinary avatar loading is unaffected.

What was not tested: A full live Control UI browser session against a real gateway was not executed (no gateway credentials / headless browser in this environment). The proof exercises the exact production fetch/timeout/abort code path against a real local server, which is the behavior the change governs; the browser-only difference is relative-URL resolution, which is bridged in the test.
